My strange sertraline experience 
I was prescribed 50 mg of Sertraline last August. At first, it made my anxiety and panic attacks significantly worse and more intense, which I was told was normal since things often get worse before they get better. However, after a couple of months, I still noticed no improvement, so my GP increased the dosage. Even after that, there was no change, so the dose was eventually increased to 200 mg. That’s when I began experiencing some strange and unsettling side effects. Despite this, I stayed on the medication, believing it was just part of the process, especially since my GP advised me to continue.

One of the first side effects I noticed was memory loss—I began forgetting things frequently, and my attention span decreased dramatically. Then came something much more frightening: episodes where I would feel completely "frozen." At random times during the day, I would suddenly be unable to move or speak, as if my body had shut down, and I’d zone out from reality, sometimes for over an hour. It was terrifying. My mum (if she was around) would just have to sit beside me until the episode passed because I couldn’t come out of it. Sometimes these episodes were shorter, like five minutes, but they often occurred in clusters. I'd become 'un-frozen' only to become trapped again soon after.

I finally tapered off Sertraline in March this year, doing it very slowly to avoid the usual withdrawal effects people often experience when coming off SSRIs. Surprisingly, I didn't notice any of the typical withdrawal symptoms. However, around that time, I began experiencing sudden fainting spells, something I had never experienced before in my life. We think it might have been related to an issue with the vagus nerve (VVS), especially since it was accompanied by intense abdominal cramping. Although I still get that sensation occasionally, it's much less severe now and without the pain.

The “frozen” episodes have reduced in intensity since then, and I do feel better—not like my old self, but definitely better than when I was on the medication. Still, it's almost September now, and I continue to experience these episodes a few times each month. My short-term memory is still significantly impaired since taking Sertraline. I forget things constantly and have lost nearly all motivation—I’ve never felt like this before. I used to be extremely self-disciplined, but now I struggle to tackle anything challenging. It feels like my brain is only capable of chasing easy or quick dopamine hits, like sugar, and my dermatillomania has worsened considerably. I’m exhausted all the time.

My loved ones have all noticed a difference between who I was before and after taking Sertraline, and I wish I’d never started it. I feel frustrated that my GP didn’t advise me to stop earlier and instead kept increasing the dose. I trusted him, as I was desperate to feel better, but looking back, it wasn’t the best decision. I also still feel emotionally numb.

I genuinely feel like my brain has been 'damaged' in some way? I hope I can recover... but it feels like I'm making such slow progress and at times no progress with regards to my memory and attention span. This was my gap year, and I start uni in mid September, so I’m kind of worried about how this will affect my academics.

A couple of weeks ago, I talked to my godmother about this, and she told me about her husband's experience. He was prescribed Sertraline several years ago for anxiety and agoraphobia, and it caused him to go into toxic shock. Initially, they weren't sure if Sertraline was the cause, so he stopped taking it. However, two weeks later, he started taking it again, and within a few days, he went into toxic shock once more. He made a good recovery afterwards thankfully.

I haven’t met anyone who’s experienced these effects with Sertraline. Has anyone here had a similar experience?

Re trying sertraline, please help
To give a bit of background. Im a 21 Y/O Male (UK) ive been really struggling with GI issues for the past 3 years. Nausea, bloating, cramping, dull pain etc. And have had next to every test to figure out what it is. Ultrasounds. CT scans, Endoscopy (With no anesthesia. Wouldnt reccomend), Diet changes, Lifestyle changes. The list goes on.

And throughout all of this all that was found was a small hiatal hernia which is a bit of a pain when it comes to heartburn but it dosent really cause me any issues. 

This has really destroyed my life. I have tried 2-3 times to get back to work but it dosent really last too long as the ammount of sick days i end up pulling just gets me fired or forces me to quit. And amongs all the other things like socialising, relationships etc. It has basically crippled me with depression/ health anxiety. 

Sertraline part:

Now, my issue is my doctor suspects that i might not have any stomach issues at all and that it may be a form of anxiety making me feel sick and causing these stomach pains for me. And that it could be entirely mental. I Never thought id be the type of person to have anxiety. At heart im a massive extrovert. I ride motorbikes. I could speak infront of 100 people and feel next to no anxiety about it. I can speak to women and friends with no issues. Etc. But i am also aware anxiety can come in different forms i guess. But now i am starting to wonder if sertraline may be my answer to fix my life and get rid of these stomach problems and get me back to work and enjoying life for the first time in years without the worry of, Should i eat this, Is it too late to eat, Is that too much exercise, Will that make me feel sick.

A few months ago i took half of my first 50mg tablet and felt like i was going to throw up for a week straight and never touched them again. I am at a point in life where i have just left a 4 year relationship 2 ish weeks ago and could really really do with at least testing how this medication could help me as i still have the sertraline and was thinking about taking a 25mg dose and sticking to it this time but again i am extremely worried about the nausea. 

How do people deal with this? It says i should take them in the morning with food but is before i go to sleep better? should i try and start on a smaller dose than 25mg? Is taking them with water better than food? Do anti sickness meds help? Im am very susceptible to nausea as it is and also have emitophobia.

In short any advice for the nausea would be tremendously helpful and if anyone else suffers with a similar thing to me i would really love to hear about it.
 Thanks.

Help - brain fog?? ssri/benzo
Hello,
I’ve recently been prescribed sertraline 50mg - going on day 12 for GAD/panic anxiety. I have experienced severe (what I think it’s called) brain fog prior to being medicated. I would suffer this brain fog and dizziness and it would cause me to panic. It feels like pressure on the head specifically the front. It causes me to think about it constantly and it’s hard to think of anything else because it’s so debilitating. I feel like I can’t think straight ever! This is also not constant and happens probably 4-6 days of the week. Anyway, I was given a script for clonazepam to get me through the horrific side effects sertraline has. I’ve noticed clonazepam completely takes away this brain fog and makes me feel like a normal person again with no anxiety/depression and makes me feel hopeful vs hopeless majority of the time. I didn’t even think I suffered depression until starting sertraline. My question is once sertraline becomes therapeutic will it help this brain fog since it has to do with anxiety? Has anyone experienced this?

is my ADHD med not working bc hormones??
Background/stressors: 
29F. Since 2018 I’ve taken sertraline 200mg for OCD & PTSD. lamotrigine 150mg for mood. smoked weed heavy from ages 22-29 (finally quit this Oct!) Nexplanon inserts since I was 17. 

2017-19 worked at a group home & witnessed many traumas. went from 170lb to 200lb. 

Summer ‘22 dx w/fructose malabsorption. 

Jan ‘23 dx w/sleep apnea. 
Got to +180-185lbs, mostly in my face & midsection, which is hard to lose. dvlp'd papules & cysts on my cheeks & thought was an allergic reaction to CPAP fabric straps. 

Apr ‘23, moved out mom’s house & adjusted to life w/ long-term bf. My closest childhood friend was dying & in an abusive living situation, but I couldn’t help her. 

Summer ‘23 finally dx w/ADHD. 

aug 9 '23 started ADD 10mg XR.

sept 1 '23 up to 20mg while
pursuing a competitive grad school for an ambitious major with no prerequisites (carpe diem, right?)

sept 6 '23 I contacted dermatitis (most likely poison ivy) between my nethers! prescribed prednisone 20mg so 21 pills over 14 days & definitely had some baby hypomanic episodes—many goal-oriented bxs & honestly extended myself too far… 
after work I had nothing left in me to get household stuff done & slept a lot so oct '23 my NP added ADD 10mg IR for an afternoon boost.

I almost completely lost my appetite & got to 170lbs!!! My memory retention was amazing. Had impeccable focus, confidence, witty, moved gracefully and swiftly, no clumsiness—but compulsions got worse. 

Lots of cleaning, which I normally hate. started making off the cuff jokes at work & briefly talked abt religion (prob reviewing my Bible course notes) w/coworkers--not my baseline. 

Then 3 days w/o sleep. couldn’t stop fidgeting. had so much energy and verve. I wanted to run across the city. had awesome ideas I had to hurry up & write down. I felt great, but my intuition knew something wasn’t right & i held onto reality for dear life. Lots of crying.

I would sit in the mirror & pick at my acne for hours. I would sort & file all my college notes (10 yrs worth) to finesse my grad school app (to connect underlying themes of my classes to suffice lack of prerequisites). I was even in a mentorship program to help w/grad school.

nov 29 '23 my therapist saw me tweaking out & had my NP stop the ADD. A whole week cold turkey. quite a crash. 

dec 8 '23 I watched my close friend get taken off life support and die. Shortly after, we started Vyvanse 40mg. 

this jan-may Vyv +50mg but didn’t feel much diff. My working memory sucked. Low motivation. Confidence tanked. didn’t get into the prestigious grad school—not surprised, just pained the dream was dead.

In March '24, my NP pulled me from work for a month long sabbatical. Applied to another well renowned grad school. 

This June - Vyv 60mg but still didn’t l see improvement. 
After 3 mo my NP was concerned about my low self-esteem (spoiler alert—didnt get into the renowned grad school either) & my wt plateaued at 175lbs.

This Sept we restarted ADD 20mg but I had to tell her asap if I didnt get enough sleep/goal-oriented compulsions. 

Late Oct I had the worst weed induced panic attack & quit cold turkey. Ive had no interest since so late Nov she agreed to ADD +25mg. 

Currently, don’t feel sharp like the 1st time. Focus is back & confidence is better. taking a break from applying to grad school. motivation still low. I dont want to do anything if I dont have to. Working memory is ok but visual fatigue is heavy. I immediately forget where I put things. My spatial awareness still sucks. Inattentive symptoms most concerning. Overall theres not that much brain fog, but still tired a lot. 

Interestingly, my appetite increased! I believe its mostly circumstantial bc Im stressed tf out!! Being an adult is fucking hard! cant save money, still cant drive, cant take care of my cats & my living situation is... complicated. Ive found refuge in sugar (goddamn fructose) & GAINED 10lbs since I restarted adderall!!!!! 

I still sit in the mirror & pick at my acne (1x/2x weekly) but I have a good face regimen so it doesnt look nearly as bad but its taking forever to heal… my NP knows, but she’s cautious about increasing adderall

In Sept, we started guanfacine 1mg to help w/the PTSD (hypervigilance) & +2mg last week.

a month ago, I noticed neck hair growing, peach fuzz growing back faster & darker. eyebrows have gotten thicker… 

due to nexplanon I cant be certain my irregular periods are abnormal so im seeing an OBGYN next month for  possible PCOS

This past Sept I was due for a new nexplanon insert but doc said its still good for 2 yrs which Ive read abt but idk

any theories, suggestions abt why adderall isnt working the same this time? or personal experiences that could give insight to my novella? thanks!

Hello, I'm not sure what's happening to me and I could really use some help.

Friday 3am I woke up with nausea and UTI symptoms. The UTI pain was the most extreme I've ever experienced so saw an out of hours GP at 5am where I was prescribed the usual trimethoprim. For the rest of the day I felt extremely drained likely from lack of sleep.

Saturday 11am I woke up after 12 hours of sleep feeling good. I had a bowl of cereal and a coffee, and then about an hour later I started experiencing all the symptoms above, minus the panic attack. 

Saturday 3pm after 3 hours of sitting on the bathroom floor I phoned 111 (UK non-emergency healthcare) who advised I attend A&E. Partner took me there, but all my vitals came back normal including blood oxygen 100%. Out of hours GP appointment scheduled for the evening. I struggled to walk back to the car because of my breathing and legs feeling like jelly.

Saturday 9pm I had the GP appointment where again my vitals were fine and they said it was probably anxiety but also that I needed to insist my regular GP do my thyroid function test ASAP (see below). At that time I was feeling anxious, but I wasn't feeling anxious earlier in the day.

When I got home, I had a full blown panic attack. I don't have them often. I managed to get some sleep, waking up in the night very often with a pounding chest and anxiety, but I slept. The first few minutes after I woke up I felt actually good and normal, but then the chest feeling kicked in again and is still present as I type.

I've never had anxiety or panic attacks lasting 24 hours before, especially not after sleeping. Is this really what is happening to me or could there be an actual medical cause?

Other things maybe of note:
- I had a case of BPPV last weekend and at the doctors on Monday my blood pressure was low for the first time in my life. 90 over something, sorry can't remember exactly.
- My annual thyroid function test is 3 months overdue because my GP surgery is facing a backlog. My dose hasn't changed in years though.
- About 1-2 times a month I'll wake up in the night feeling really nauseous and often throw up. When I do, I'm not able to get back to sleep because my body jerks me awake. This has been going on for about 6 months.

Thank you

chest pain from sertraline
I (19M) take sertraline for OCD. At the end of August, my dose was increased from 150mg to 200mg. The high dose of Zoloft gave me several side effects, one of which was chest pain, and I went back down to 150mg after 3 days. 

I talked to my doctor and she said since wasn’t having any side effects on 150mg or any other dose, the side effects would go away after at most 2 weeks. She ordered a blood test to check my troponin levels but my dad (a nurse) said she only did that because I have health anxiety and she wanted to get rid of me. He also said that troponin would have normalized already and so he threw the requisite away. 

The chest pain hasn’t gone away several months later. Most of the time I’m fine but right before bed I start feeling a pressure/stabbing pain in my sternum and over to the right side, sometimes in my actual heart too. It generaly gets worse with exercise. Not enough to really disrupt me but enough that I notice it. A few nights ago, it was really bad and the pain was in my right shoulder too and I considered calling an ambulance thinking I was having a heart attack but the pain went away in about 20 minutes so I didn’t. 

I can’t tell if this is cardiovascular pain or something else because it’s not often in my heart or on the left side of my chest; it’s mostly on the right side. I only take about 5-6 thousand steps a day and occasionally smoke (I stopped in September because the chest pain), but I’m also 19 so I feel like heart disease is unlikely, especially because this only started as a side effect of Zoloft 

I talked to my dad about it a bit and he says a bit a chest pain in normal and nothing to worry about but I also feel like he’s desensitized from working in the icu because he didn’t want me to go to the hospital after hitting my arm with an axe a few years ago. He says it’s just my ocd talking when I’m anxious about it and it very well could be but like… my chest hurts and I never got the blood test my doctor ordered to check for heart damage. I also feel like I’m pretty good at discerning if pain is caused by anxiety or if it’s real

I have an appointment with my psychiatrist in January where I plan to start weaning off Zoloft and try something else. I haven’t been able to get an appointment with my GP because she only books 3 weeks in advance and is full into the new year. I went to a walk in clinic and the doctor took my pulse and oxygen levels then said im fine and sent me home. Im pretty sure that because I have OCD on my chart he wasnt super concerned about my chest pain and didnt order bloodwork or imagaing or anything like I was hoping he would even though ive had this for 4 months now and feel like something is going on.

How concerned should I be? Should the chest pain go away once I stop taking Sertraline or is this indicative of something more serious?

2+ Months of Coughing - Dr Cant Find Cause
Chronic Cough - Dr Cant Find Reason For It

About 2 months ago I started to have this persistent dry cough come on. I was not sick before or when it started. I was feeling otherwise perfectly fine.

After 2 weeks of having the cough and no other symptoms, I went to my GP. GP gave me some cough suppressant meds and some nasal spray to see if they helped. She also gave me a Z-Pack with the instructions to take it if the other medications did not help after a few days.

Neither medication helped at all so I started taking the Z-Pack about 5 days later. For the first 3 days that I took the Z-Pack tablets, I felt increasingly better. Then on day 4, it was like all progress was lost and I was right back to coughing the same as before. The last day was no different.

At about the month mark, I went back to my GP and got chest X-rays done to check for pneumonia and cancer. Results were negative for both.

GP gave me a steroid inhaler which I have been using for the last 3 weeks. While it did seem to help at first, its effectiveness seems to have worn off. My GP directed me to a specialist should the inhaler not work after 2 weeks.

The problem is, the timing landed me smack dab in the week between Christmas and NY so the specialist’s office is closed until the 2nd.

I came down with a cold on Christmas morning (Merry Christmas to me!) and the cough has gotten worse because of it. My chest is almost always somewhere on the spectrum between discomfort and pain and I sometimes feel like I am breathing through a straw - not so much that I cant catch my breath but enough for me to notice and for it to be somewhat uncomfortable.

Because of my cold, I have had to call out of work several days now and will likely need to do so at least once or twice more before it clears up. But I suspect the cough will remain which is a problem. I thought about going to urgent care today because I don’t want to wait until the 2nd (realistically longer as I will have to call and make an appointment on the 2nd and I doubt that it will be on the same day). But, upon reading what my local urgent care can and cannot do, Im not sure they would be able to do anything my GP hasn’t already tried.

So, I am left with either going to the ER, which I think is overkill, or waiting it out until I can see this specialist.

Im really tired of coughing and not having anything work to stop it. And I am worried about the cough lasting for so long and making my chest hurt. It literally came out of nowhere and has hung around for no discernible reason. I have googled every possible combination of words I can think of to try and find possibilities for what it could be but I just get the same few that just don’t fit. Im not a smoker and never have been. I don’t have asthma. I do deal with some postnasal drip and general stuffiness but it’s never caused anything like this before. Cough is largely dry and unproductive. My throat is often raw from the coughing. I don’t cough as much when I am eating.

Disclaimer: I know nobody on here can diagnose this and I am going to see this specialist so no need to tell me to do so. I just am looking for something to get me through the interim until I can see that specialist.

25F. Only medication Sertraline 100mg for 3 years roughly. I’m in the UK but not whether this is relevant.

Hi, this might be a bit longwinded but I want to include all details of steps I have taken and what not. 

Since September I have had very sore nostrils that were obviously infected, I thought it was caused by dry/cold air from the weather changing so was using Vaseline. This wasn’t working so I went to my GP, no nasal swab was taken but I was prescribed Naseptin to use for 7/10 days (can’t remember duration sorry) this cleared it all up whilst I was using it until I stopped and the soreness would come back. I just kept using the Naseptin until I got fed up of it and went to my GP again who swabbed my nostrils this time, and I tested positive for Staph and have just finished with Fucidic acid cream (only 2 days ago have I finished so can’t say for certain whether it has put a stop to the recurring infection) but my nostrils have been fine the last few days so I’m hoping that’s it. 

But, and I’m not sure if it’s related, my lips have been also very sore since October roughly. Started off at the corner of my lips which cleared up but spread to my bottom lip. The symptoms of this are basically my lips feel very chapped as if their dry and are constantly peeling. I have a birth mark type of thing on my bottom lip and this seems to be the most irritated as in the area around that, it has bled and has also been weeping slightly. No pus just clear liquid, and not constant just when my lips are at their most irritated. My lips feel hot and maybe even slightly swollen but this isn’t visible, and to even just look at my lips I can’t see any visible signs of anything at all apart from tiny bits of peeling skin which are barely noticeable. My GP said he doesn’t believe this is related to the infection in my nostrils and that my lips are just dry, and I do tend to get dry lips sometimes, particularly when I have nasal congestion but this doesn’t feel familiar in that way.

The only thing that actually works and completely clears it up is Hydrocortisone which I have been using very regularly recently, which I of course need to stop doing but it is the only thing that has helped so far and I’ve been pretty desperate. I have used aquaphor going along with what my GP said about them being dry and I think any thing that moisturises my lips actually make it worse. I used Naseptin which was only meant for my nostrils but I tried that and it helped a very small amount. Also the Fusidic acid cream I have been putting on my lower lip for the last few days and this has not made any difference to it at all. These episodes don’t happen when I haven’t eaten, if anything they’ve seemed to only ever happen about 4 hours after a meal. I had my fit bit on during the last episode I had, and my resting bpm reached a peak 120, and fluctuated in the 100s for about 30min before gradually going down

Feel free to give me any input or ask any further questions.

Chronic Bad Breath
Age: 43

Gender: Male

Height: 5'11"

Weight: 180lbs

Smoker: No (Never have been)

Duration: 12+ years. Possibly my whole life.

Location of Issue: Mouth. Possibly related to sinuses or gut health.

Medications:   
Sertraline for depression and anxiety.  I did not take it through this whole period of having bad breath.  
Azelastine HCI nasal spray for "non-allergic rhinitis".

  
My wife notices that I have unreasonably bad breath. It lingers after brushing, mouth rinse, drinking water. Eating and drinking water does seem to make it better. Anxiety seems to make it worse. It seems very prominent if I only drink coffee and not water. She said sometimes it is at a 10 on a 1-10 scale. When that happens, I'm emanating the smell when I talk, even from a distance. It only ever gets down to a 2 or a 3 at best. She says it is always something she can smell when she gets close to me.

It has been around since we began our relationship 12 years ago and she considered not dating me because of it. We don't talk about it a lot because it is uncomfortable and she felt judgy and knows I was self-conscious. She says it doesn't smell like regular bad breath from just hygiene.

A few things to note:

Brushing teeth, flossing, and using mouth rinse does not make it go away. It does mask it to an extent, but does not fully alleviate it. It is present even when my oral hygiene is perfect.

I'm always thirsty. I can drink three big 40oz cups of water and my mouth will feel swampy.I was tested for diabetes and it came back negative.

I have sinus issues. I've always dealth with what I thought were allergy problems. I often have the sniffles at any given time. Sometimes it feels like my nose is a faucet that someone turned on.  Last year around this time I was having what I thought were 3+ allergy attacks a day. It was the worst it had ever been. I finally went to an allergist and after a back-prick test was told I was not allergic to anything and instead had "non-allergic rhinitis" and was given a nasal spray. It was like night and day.  I took it consistently for a few weeks and my attacks went away and I had so many fewer nasal issues. I felt like a normal person.  Now I still have some issues and take it as necessary. I've noticed more congestion and drainage since the cold weather has come on.

I suffer from anxiety. I am managing it mentally and trying not to let it rule my decisions. (When I was younger, social anxiety would keep me from being able to do things like go to the grocery store by myself, but that is long past.) I take a small dose of sertraline to take the edge off, but I can feel it present in my body at many times, and often I don't know what's causing it.

I can't smell the bad breath. When it is very bad I can notice an intense swampiness in my mouth, but for the most part I'm oblivious. I had even thought it went away after the nasal spray treatment.

I've asked other people close to me about the bad breath. Some have noticed it and others haven't at all. I do remember ex partners mentioning it sometimes but I had thought it was just normal bad breath and would just go brush my teeth or do a mouth rinse.  Once again, I think they may not have wanted to talk about it as it is a bit of a offensive subject.

I've asked multiple doctors and dentists about it. They thought it might be throat stones. I've had a few of those but not very often. They suggested mouth wash, but that just masks it as I mentioned.

I think it may begin in my gut or related to my sinuses. I want to visit a professional that can understand what's going on and help but I'm not sure where to start. The doctors I've talked to haven't taken it very seriously and they obviously don't want to smell my breath to see if it's "normal".

Any advice you can offer would be greatly appreciated!

I have had 4 holters monitors, an echocardiogram, TTT and lots of EKGs and blood work. I'm 25f 165lbs 5'7 and have PD, GAD, IBS, asthma and take labatelol and a prenatal.

My holters have shown a high HR of 184 bpm. My cardiologist reassured me there is NOTHING wrong with my heart and this could be a severe case of panic disorder due to me stopping my sertraline 2 years ago. This started about 6 months after I stopped and gradually got worse. I am 10 weeks pregnant currently.

People on my childs father's side (previous child not this one's father) have said my heart could give out if I keep it. They try so hard to get me to abort it and even offering to drive me out of state to pay for it. I've tried to explain to them that they've found NOTHING wrong. And while my cardiologist says she doesn't like my HR getting this high, that it would take many years of this to cause damage or harm me and that it won't kill me. (Hoping she's right). I don't think she can run anymore tests as they've seen my heart in action when beating that fast. Panic attacks can worsen, change, become more frequent and last longer when untreated from what I've read. But they make it seem like this isn't normal and there's something wrong with me.

I understand that pregnancy is a big stress test for the body but wouldn't my cardiologist have warned me? I finally see my OB for the first time this week. Hormones trigger my anxiety and so I've been dizzy, SOB, light headed and a little heart racy but I explain it's normal. They are giving me anxiety over this. I feel like if they are right then more mothers would die because I'm sure as hell not the only one on earth with severe panic disorder or SVT. It took so long for me to finally accept what the Drs were saying and accepting that I'm okay but this is hard to hear all the time. I'm starting to wonder about all of this all over again .

Help! Friend Suffering Acute Pain - Meds Not Helping
Help needed please! We are located in the UK. My friend is suffering severe pain following an acute onset of neck and back spasms. Pain meds are not helping. Not sure where to go next

Background
My friend (27F) has a history of cPTSD with anxiety and depression for which she takes meds (sertraline and propranolol). She finds physical pain and discomfort distressing at the best of times. She has a relatively sedimentary lifestyle (office job, lots of time in bed because of depression) and a somewhat poor diet (lots of carbs and processed food). 

She suffered whiplash as a child falling down a hill. She occasionally gets spasms in her neck and tightness as a result.

Pertinent Medical History
On Monday at the end of her working day she developed a tension headache at the base of her skull radiating down her neck. She recognised the onset of spasms she has had before and went to a sports masseuse she occasionally uses on Tuesday. They did a general massage and cupping. Pain persisted so on Tuesday evening she spoke to the out of hours doctor who prescribe Naproxen to be take twice daily. 

Her own doctor called her on Wednesday and reassured her that the Naproxen would help. By the evening she was in severe distress, the pain and spasms are to the left of her upper spine and in her left shoulder with pain radiating under her left arm and under her breast. This makes breathing painful which in turn is causing further distress as she feels she cannot get a full lung of air. She cannot sleep on her left side or back. Being on her right side is only tolerable for short periods of time.

Spoke to the out of ours doctor on Wednesday evening. A paramedic was sent as she mentioned her chest pains (standard procedure it seems for the guys who triage the calls). ECG normal, blood pressure normal (I want to say 120/90), sats at >95%, GCS 15. The doctor prescribed Codeine (1-2 pills four times a day) and Diazepam (1 pill three times a day) and advised her to keep using Naproxen twice a day and Paracetamol. 

Taken to A&E Thursday afternoon and examined by a doctor. Again, normal obs. Urine sample checked (assume pregnancy). Examination conducted - doctor identified extremely painful areas in her back spasming. Doctor advised to use cold (she had been using heat) and to double up on the diazepam to two pills. 

Since managed to get a few hours sleep and since Thursday evening has been taking 2x Diazepam every 8 hours, 2x codeine every six hours, 1x Naproxen every 12 hours, plus the maximum dose of Paracetamol (8 tablets in 24 hours with at least four hours between doses). 

Still there is no let up and she is extremely distressed. She says no one is listening to her. The pain comes in waves with her discomfort at 6/10 at all times, rising to 10/10 when it spasms or she has to move. She has probably slept about eight hours total in the past four days. She is crying constantly and yelping when she has to move or it spasms. 

Objectively I can state I have never seen her like this in the past five years I have known her. It’s heartbreaking and as much as I’m trying to reassure her that the issue needs to just run its course, I am really worried for her, especially due to her mental health. 

Her neuro obs seem ok - no loss of sensation, no tingling, no issues with bladder or bowel control, no loss of feeling, no confusion apart from a general frazzled brain as you’d expect from someone not sleeping g properly for a week. No known injury, cuts or bruising (other than the cupping marks). She has had a light period for several weeks due to recently starting the pill (can’t remember the name but it’s a combined type, 3 weeks on, 1 week off). 

Occam’s razor tells me this is probably what it says on the tin - a particularly nasty case of non-specific upper back pain, probably due to poor posture and lifestyle. But is there anything that might have been missed and is there anything else that can be done? I want to advocate for her as she is struggling to articulate herself and make herself heard to doctors.  Would strong meds, muscle relaxants or even sleeping meds be considered in this circumstance, especially given her mental vulnerability? Is there any further diagnostic tests that might help?

19F - heavy period after Nexplanon
Hi! Thanks in advance for reading. 

I am F19, white, about 5’3 and 120-130 pounds. I have no diagnoses besides anemia (got iron infusion for a year ago) as well as suspected endometriosis. Also suspected IBS. 

I take 50mg sertraline for anxiety following a traumatic event.

It caused around 100 days of straight bleeding, as well as extreme cramps, ultra heavy (1 tampon/ pad every hour, literally was considering adult diapers) bleeding, nausea, brain fog, heart palpitations and fatigue. I posted this on Askpsychiatry but it didnt get much traction. 

tldr. I developed an allergy to one of my depression meds, but it was the most effective one I have tried so far. I asked my psyc for an allergy test just to confirm it wasn't triggered by an inactive ingredient, but she pushed for me to do a Genesight test instead. Additionally, I believe I may be experiencing some negative side effects triggered by taking sertraline and Adderall together, but my psyc doesnt believe they would cause such things. I don't know if I'm overreacting to my new meds interacting and if an allergy test is a waste of time in comparison to Genesight. 

I had an allergic reaction to bupropion after increasing my dose (1 75mg to 1.5 75mg), but so far it has been the most effective depression medication I have tried. Within a week of upping my bupropion dose I woke up one morning with an extremely hoarse voice that was unrecognizable. I jokingly called it a 50 pack a day, 20 years smoker's voice. I made a telehealth appointment the next day with my psyc and she told me it was an allergic reaction. I took a Benadryl that night and I was back to normal within a few days. I didn't have hives which she was most concerned about.

This happened last December and since I have been on sertraline varying from 25-50mg based on adjustments from my psychiatrist. It seems that every week or so I experience a new negative side effect, but finally this week I think the increased levels of anxiety and depression I felt at first have started to even out. Now the most pressing negative side effects seem to all be physical and is most apparent on days I take my 30mg generic adderall. Additionally, since starting sertraline the adderall seems way less effective and even taking an additional half a pill in the afternoon doesn't help. My Dr. suggested doubling the adderall at first, but I declined, sighting that if my original dose worked before sertraline then I don't want to just up it for a medicine that I don't seem to benefit from. She then said to take the two 30 minutes apart and two weeks in I don't feel any changes. I dug around on the internet trying to find some info that could give me hope because I didn't realize how much better my mental state was with bupropion. So, for my most recent appointment I asked if it would be possible to get an allergy test done for all the ingredients in the generic bupropion I used in case it was an inactive ingredient that triggered the reaction. She didn't really seem to consider it much. Instead, she said that she would like to have me do a Genesight swab. She doesn't know of any interactions between sertraline and adderall and has admitting to being stumped to what depression med to try next. Additionally, she wrote me a script for Vyvanse after I asked if there was something we could change in the meantime. She said vyvanse and adderall are different enough that it is possible I won't have the same reactions. These physical reactions are feeling hot, sometimes sweating more than usual, extreme dry mouth, almost a tingly feeling all over, and kind of feeling my chest. Sorry, I know the last two points may sound weird, but I'm not too sure how to describe the sensations. They are not painful or unbearable... just weird to be tingling all over for hours. These physical reactions do inhibit my ability to focus. Unless I have a clearly defined task and deadline, I feel very scattered and brain foggy. Taking my xanax or getting a kratom drink significantly helps, but I don't like the idea of taking something to make a medication bearable you know?  


So, I suppose I'm wondering how worth it Genesight would be? I've never heard of it before and thankfully told my psychiatrist I would like to think about it before committing to the \~$300 test. It seems like it would tell her what medications may or may not be as effective rather than information on what I am allergic to? I understand that she doesn't want me to have another allergic reaction, but will Genesight provide any info related to that?

Also, after just a quick google search online I saw that there is a major chance of interactions with using adderall (or vyvanse) and sertraline together. I didn't want to bring this up though because I don't know what is considered a "major interaction" and I'm not in the medical field. Should I be cautious about these together?

I am currently prescribed sertraline 25 mg, xanax 0.5 mg, adderall 30 mg, and vyvanse 20 mg (I haven't picked these up yet), all generic. In the past I have tried aripiprazole, fluoxetine, and bupropion. I stopped aripiprazole because I didn't notice any changes with it and stopped fluoxetine because it killed my libido.

 Hi everyone, I'm Rex a 19-year-old guy who is in a tough spot and needs your help. Sorry if this is long. Well, my story goes like this,

Since childhood, I have been daydreaming a lot. I would create imaginary characters and roles to satisfy what I couldn't do in real life but apparently, intrusive thoughts kept popping up in my mind and kept messing up my imagination. To quiet down these intrusive thoughts I would have to repeatedly imagine myself fighting a figure which represents my intrusive thoughts. I would have to do this every time I had an intrusive thought to neutralize it to the point it wouldn’t let me focus on the real world. In October 2021, I started receiving these sudden attacks of palpitations, sweating, difficulty breathing, dry throat, sudden depressive mood + thoughts, and racing thoughts for 10-12 hours a day. Other than these the thoughts got more intrusive, increased in frequency, and increased in the time they lasted. Every time I fail to neutralize these thoughts they change my personality and control me. Hard to explain how, it’s like experiencing a 6th feeling. Whenever these thoughts come they separate you from reality, it feels like you are in a separate universe that lasts for an hour.

I finally got diagnosed with anxiety in Nov 2021 for which I was given Clonazepam .75mg and Sertraline 50mg per day. The treatment did help initially but it soon became worse. Especially in the morning, I would violently jerk my head because of the distress I would have due to the thoughts I was dealing with. I got in contact with a Psychiatrist and he diagnosed me with OCD for which he reduced clonazepam, increased sertraline to 150 mg slowly, and induced risperidone .5 mg. Risperidone was a magic pill, all other pills would just reduce the symptoms whereas risperidone solved the problem as soon as it was consumed. But its positive effects slowly wore off to the point it started having no effect. Over 6 months, I was put on Fluoxetine (40mg), Fluvoxamine (150mg), Buspirone (20mg), and Haloperidol (don’t remember the dosage but had some positive effect when taken the first time but not any further).

My health took a turn for the worse when I got food poisoning and my mood became highly depressive (felt more like biological depression than psychological) and the intensity of the thoughts reached a peak. I became crippled to the point I couldn’t even wear clothes or eat food by myself. They wouldn’t let me. I got in contact with a different Psychiatrist, and he too diagnosed me with OCD for which he started me on Amisulpride 25 mg which worked well, he induced clomipramine 25mg and gradually increased Amisulpride to 100mg. When I recovered from food poisoning he increased clomipramine to 150mg and waited for 3 months, it gave no result. Then he increased it to 225mg which showed mild improvement but he had to reduce it back to 150mg because of its side effects and increased fluvoxamine to 300 mg but again no result.

In this period, I started seeing visuals, voices, and sensations. Whenever a thought would be too intense I could actually see it, especially in a dark room, not in high detail but like 2d stickers pasted on my field of view. I would rarely hear voices at night which other people won’t. The most distressing of them would be physical sensations, I would feel physical discomfort not only on my skin but anywhere in my body including internal areas, and would have to create barriers in my imagination to neutralize it. I brought these up to my Psychiatrist but he said that these are not hallucinations but only OCD thoughts. He tried Vortioxetine, Escitalopram, Venlafaxine, Aripiprazole, Olanzapine, and Paroxetine but none of them helped.

I got in contact with another Psychiatrist and he suggested Deep TMS (Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation). I got around 40 sessions of Deep TMS therapy but again it showed nearly no positive effect. The doctor, asks me to wait for about a year for the results to show up. I’ve been feeling unreasonably depressed and suicidal for the past 2 weeks. When I told this to my doctor he just made a few changes to the meds, it felt as if he ignored my point while he just asked me to wait.

Update (To the original post): About 6 years ago I used to firmly believe that there are some divine signs of god and I have have some serious divine purpose and need to act upon it up to the point my daily life decisons would be based on the events whether I saw a pigeon on my left window or didn't find my slipper (sounds stupid but that's how it was). I also believe that the imaginary world is not real but it represents something which is real which means all my obsessions and compulsions are rational and reasonable. I also talk to dead objects like the bed, helmet and think they might have feelings.

What do I do? 

P.S.: I’ve exhausted CBT, ERP, and a few other meds; none of them worked.

As previously stated, my neurological symptoms began in 11/2022 and have continued to progress since then. At first my neurologist didn’t think my Chiari malformation was the cause, but after the drawn out process of ruling out so much else and certain symptoms (like balance issues and headaches at the base of my skull) getting worse, I was referred to a neurosurgeon and finally able to meet with him a month and a half ago (early December). He determined based on my symptoms and my imaging showing my cerebellar tonsils extending 15-18mm into my neck (down to my C2 vertebra) that the chiari 1 malformation was almost certainly causing a fair amount of my symptoms and I was an excellent candidate for surgery in his next available time. Unfortunately, due to a change in insurance coverage he would not be able to be the one performing the surgery and it’s been a mess trying to get referred elsewhere (through no fault of that neurosurgeon’s practice). I finally have an appointment scheduled for July to meet with a spine clinic at a hospital, who will then refer me to neurosurgery, who will require a consultation with them before scheduling surgery. 

I’m not just frustrated about another 6 months of waiting around to try to get help for this, I’m really concerned about how much worse my symptoms will get in that time based on where they’re at already.

As of now, my base level of pain is around a 4/10 on average, with most days including headache and/or nerve pain flaring up and exceeding 6/10. I get dizzy and lightheaded just from showering or walking through the grocery store. I’m incredibly easily fatigued and struggling with insomnia (which is such a vicious cycle). My arm and hand strength has weakened to the point that I can’t always lift a full gallon of milk to pour from it and sometimes pick up a glass of water only to have to put it back down immediately because my hand feels like it’s going to drop it. My memory is now poor at best, with me often unknowingly repeating questions or relaying the same information over and over. My cognitive processing is slowing down at a noticeable rate and I’ve been told by family that I’m now regularly mixing up or misusing words I’ve known and used properly since I was a teenager. The pain at the base of my skull/top of my neck is getting worse. And most concerning to me: I have started having noticeable fatigue in my mouth and throat muscles resulting in very slowed eating and difficulty swallowing to the point I’m able to swallow my Gabapentin in the morning and manage it in the afternoon if I eat something after, but have to cut it in quarters to take it at night. Some nights I even notice my diclofenac catching and trying to pushing things down with water doesn’t even work. Additionally, I’ve been noticing a sound inside my head almost like crumpling plastic when I tilt or turn my head certain ways, but it’s not accompanied by pain or dizziness or anything so I haven’t worried about that.

Ultimately, my question is: what would be red flags that tell me I need to go to the hospital?

I can’t seem to get any meaningful answers from any of my providers, searching medical articles online hasn’t helped, and I’m so accustomed to downplaying and ignoring my symptoms that I don’t trust that I would just *know* when I’ve gone from urgent to emergency. Can anyone please help me with what I should watch for? 
Thanks

All went well until the doctor dilated my eyes and saw my optical nerves were fuzzy (papilledema). He seemed freaked out and immediately sent me to the emergency eye department in the building get an MRI (over an hour) to make sure it wasn't a brain tumor. 

Luckily it wasn't. At this point, after tons of waiting around, it was around 10pm and a group of 3 doctors came in to see me, seemingly stoked to encounter someone with an uncommon condition (teaching hospital), all taking turns shining bright lights in my eyes and repeating the same tests over and over and over. They kept asking me if I had any of what I learned were the symptoms of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH). My answers were always no. Headaches that wake me up at night? No. Am I obese? No (which is a common part of the profile). Ringing in my ears? No. And on and on. I had the papilledema, but nothing else notable. They dilated my eyes again at now around 11PM at night, despite my protests, so when I was finally released later on I was on the street in the dark struggling to find my uber because everything was blurry.  

Nonetheless, my official diagnosis was IIH. They told me "you'll be coming in again next week to see the neuro-ophthalmologist and get a spinal tap, before then we need you to get bloodwork even though it's Friday night and your appointment is Tuesday, we'll start you on this medication, it's important because there's a small chance you may go blind someday in the future." They told me the bloodwork was to rule things out, and "we don't think you have any of these conditions". So I didn't even look at the bloodwork they ordered. I did not take time out of my day to go get a blood test on Monday for results that wouldn't be ready by the next day anyway. I was thankful to my optometrist for his concern, but the doctors I saw at night didn't seem to care about me at all and failed to make me understand why this was all so urgent. 

I went to my appointment on Tuesday, expecting a spinal tap. Instead, the doctor had me go get a blood test (\~10 tubes) then and there (thank goodness I didn't waste my time before...), asked me the same questions and did the same tests plus a few more for my peripheral vision, and sent me home without a spinal tap as she realized I had like zero symptoms other than the optic nerves. She scheduled my follow up for 9/1, ordered some more bloodwork and wrote the prescription for the medication Diamox. 

# Medication issues

The next day, I had an appointment with my primary care doctor who I love, and who was the only one to tell me that I shouldn't be taking spironolactone and Diamox together, even though I made sure all the doctors knew my medications.

Part of the reason I should not be taking them together are that they are both diuretics...if that is the case, why switch out one drug for the other if they do similar things???

I stopped the Spiro as of Monday and started taking the Diamox as of Tuesday, and I hate it. It makes me exhausted, gives me diarrhea, has made me stop my spironolactone so I'm terrified my hormonal acne will come back, makes my appetite even worse (my ophthalmologist didn't seem to care about my poor appetite at all and didn't even put it in my chart, and only acknowledged it when she was saying it could be a side effect of Diamox, then commented something along the lines of 'oh, you're already experiencing that'.)  

I also have been considering increasing my sertraline as my depression has been getting worse and worse, but my pdoc is currently moving offices so I haven't been able to have a full session with him since early summer...I spoke to him very briefly to updated him about my IIH diagnoses and new medication, as well as my worsening depression, and he stated he didn't know about diamox and sertraline interactions, and just upped my dose to 75 mg anyway. Since I'm already changing my meds, I'm holding off on adding the addt'l 25 until i'm on the diamox for another week or so. Again, none of my doctors alerted me about any interactions about sertraline and diamox despite me already being on Sertaline, so even though the interactions seem somewhat concerning, idk how seriously I should even take them.

My primary doctor also ordered some more bloodwork (\~8 tubes), which I completed the next day. (I had a CBC done twice, once during bloodwork on Tuesday 8/15 at the eye clinic appointment, and once on Thursday 8/17 at quest when I did the bloodwork ordered by my primary care/addt'l bloodword from ophthalmologist)

* My [white blood cells](https://imgur.com/OblPudN), [eosinophils](https://imgur.com/kqyaSMG), and [lymphocytes](https://imgur.com/Rd9jfws) were unprecedently low
   *  [Similarly low](https://imgur.com/8SDcdJW) on the test from 8/15 (not Quest)
* [Glucose](https://imgur.com/TpIhMhL) was also sliiightly high at Quest considering I fasted for over 12 hours. 
   * It was [even higher on the other CBC,](https://imgur.com/PLHuElW) on 8/15 but I cannot remember if I fasted before hand or not, and if so for how long. 
* My [B12 was within normal range](https://imgur.com/evFIBBI), but my opthalmologist made a point to tell me to take vitamins for it. 

Urine results...

* Trace ketones
* 1+ bilirubin
* Trace protein

Okay, so that was that. It was weird, and I was freaked out, but after a while I talked myself down. Then more results came in, which I didn't have a frame of reference for at all, so I committed the cardinal sin of googling them. 

* ​
* [High C-Reactive protein](https://imgur.com/URcYSnv) (I suppose expected due to inflammation) 
* [Reactive RPR test](https://imgur.com/9aHR9V1), albeit with [non-reactive treponema](https://imgur.com/vmCMshU) (again, I haven't had sex in forever so I couldn't imagine it was syphillus BUT I read a false positive may mean something else...)
* [Reactive Hep A and B](https://imgur.com/1JcBNff) (I am trying to find my vaccine record to see if I was vaccinated for them, as I heard that would show up as reactive)

By the time the reactive Hepatitis results came in, it was a week since my last appoint and I was sobbing at work because I was confused and scared. Do I need to be careful because my immune system is weak? Do I need to be careful to not give anyone hepatitis? Do I have a disease that could progress without care? Am I overreacting? At that point, it was nearly 2 weeks until my next appointment, and I was freaking out. I couldn't get a hold of my ophthalmologist or my primary care doctor, so I decided to just go to the eye clinic in person. I was able to talk to a receptionist who got in contact with my doctors assistant, who left a message for my doctor asking her to contact me ASAP; it was after 5PM at this point so I was happy to just be promised to hear from her by first thing in the morning.

I don't know if she has access to my past WBC counts for example....I don't understand how testing reactive on an RPR test is normal...I know you are not supposed to google things but when you get bombarded with all those red triangles and unintelligible technical descriptions, it's hard not to!

I stopped the Spiro as of Monday and started taking the Diamox as of Tuesday, and I hate it. It makes me exhausted, gives me diarrhea, has made me stop my spironolactone so I'm terrified my hormonal acne will come back, makes my appetite even worse (my ophthalmologist didn't seem to care about my poor appetite at all and didn't even put it in my chart, and only acknowledged it when she was saying it could be a side effect of Diamox, then commented something along the lines of 'oh, you're already experiencing that'.)  

I also have been considering increasing my sertraline as my depression has been getting worse and worse, but my pdoc is currently moving offices so I haven't been able to have a full session with him since early summer...I spoke to him very briefly to updated him about my IIH diagnoses and new medication, as well as my worsening depression, and he stated he didn't know about diamox and sertraline interactions, and just upped my dose to 75 mg anyway. Since I'm already changing my meds, I'm holding off on adding the addt'l 25 until i'm on the diamox for another week or so. Again, none of my doctors alerted me about any interactions about sertraline and diamox despite me already being on Sertaline, so even though the interactions seem somewhat concerning, idk how seriously I should even take them. 

# Bloodwork

My primary doctor also ordered some more bloodwork (\~8 tubes), which I completed the next day. (I had a CBC done twice, once during bloodwork on Tuesday 8/15 at the eye clinic appointment, and once on Thursday 8/17 at quest when I did the bloodwork ordered by my primary care/addt'l bloodword from ophthalmologist)

Then the bloodwork results began to come in, slowly, each page of results with some kind of abnormal result. Quest results allow you to compare with your prior levels, which was helpful (..?) 

As far as my CBC/metabolic panel goes; 

* On my 8/17 test results from Quest, my [cholesterol](https://imgur.com/lmNvVCl), [LDL](https://imgur.com/DZnWSck) and [Non HDL](https://imgur.com/I0duRGZ), was unprecedently high
* My [white blood cells](https://imgur.com/OblPudN), [eosinophils](https://imgur.com/kqyaSMG), and [lymphocytes](https://imgur.com/Rd9jfws) were unprecedently low
   *  [Similarly low](https://imgur.com/8SDcdJW) on the test from 8/15 (not Quest)
* [Glucose](https://imgur.com/TpIhMhL) was also sliiightly high at Quest considering I fasted for over 12 hours. 
   * It was [even higher on the other CBC,](https://imgur.com/PLHuElW) on 8/15 but I cannot remember if I fasted before hand or not, and if so for how long. 
* My [B12 was within normal range](https://imgur.com/evFIBBI), but my opthalmologist made a point to tell me to take vitamins for it. 

Urine results...

* Trace ketones
* 1+ bilirubin
* Trace protein

Okay, so that was that. It was weird, and I was freaked out, but after a while I talked myself down. Then more results came in, which I didn't have a frame of reference for at all, so I committed the cardinal sin of googling them. 

* ​
* [High C-Reactive protein](https://imgur.com/URcYSnv) (I suppose expected due to inflammation) 
* [Reactive RPR test](https://imgur.com/9aHR9V1), albeit with [non-reactive treponema](https://imgur.com/vmCMshU) (again, I haven't had sex in forever so I couldn't imagine it was syphillus BUT I read a false positive may mean something else...)
* [Reactive Hep A and B](https://imgur.com/1JcBNff) (I am trying to find my vaccine record to see if I was vaccinated for them, as I heard that would show up as reactive)

By the time the reactive Hepatitis results came in, it was a week since my last appoint and I was sobbing at work because I was confused and scared. Do I need to be careful because my immune system is weak? Do I need to be careful to not give anyone hepatitis? Do I have a disease that could progress without care? Am I overreacting? At that point, it was nearly 2 weeks until my next appointment, and I was freaking out. I couldn't get a hold of my ophthalmologist or my primary care doctor, so I decided to just go to the eye clinic in person. I was able to talk to a receptionist who got in contact with my doctors assistant, who left a message for my doctor asking her to contact me ASAP; it was after 5PM at this point so I was happy to just be promised to hear from her by first thing in the morning. 

It was even sooner! Later that night, I received the following message from my doctor:  
"I have been following up your lab works. For the lab that we already have the results, majority of them were within normal ranges, except your CRP is slightly elevated. I will continue following up your lab results. If there is anything we need to handle immediately, I will let you know. Otherwise, we will discuss your lab work on 9/1/2023. "  
I'm a sensitive person, so I may be reading too much into it, but I felt dismissed and embarrassed. I understand that she's busy and can't confer with her patients 24/7, but the slightly elevated CRP was literally the least of my worries. I don't know if she has access to my past WBC counts for example....I don't understand how testing reactive on an RPR test is normal...I know you are not supposed to google things but when you get bombarded with all those red triangles and unintelligible technical descriptions, it's hard not to!

# Questions

So, my questions are as follows..

* How serious is my diagnosis of IIH, really? Does it require medication? If so, why, if I am not experiencing any symptoms that are causing distress to me?
* Are any of my blood test results concerning to the extent that you as a doctor would prioritize talking to a patient about them?
* Even if they're not urgent, are they concerning? Will there be any follow up tests? 
* What are your opinions on adding Diamox to my current medication regimen? How about increasing my sertraline?
* Is there anything else I should know about IIH that may make me see the diagnosis in a different light?

Thank you all so much and I'm sorry that I am a bit of a hypochondriac and stubborn lol.

I’m feeling a little bit at my wits end here. They would last for about five seconds and come and go, sometimes every few minutes, other times more spaced apart. My doctor wrote them off as anxiety and suggested upping my dosage. I was hesitant at first but agreed, going from 25 to 50 mg.

These headaches lasted for about six months, and I had largely given up on seeking treatment for them. They finally stopped occurring, which I was and remain incredibly grateful for. I’m not entirely sure when the dizziness and brain fog started, but it feels like they’ve amped up over the past two weeks or so. I’ve had more trouble focusing, and I generally feel unwell (stomach issues, chills) the later I get into the day. It lasted maybe 30 seconds, but it was the first time I’ve had that happen to me.

I have chronic sinusitis and allergies but I no longer take daily allergy meds.
*Symptoms: vertigo not brought on by positional changes but made worse with movement like walking, dizziness/lightheadedness that occasionally results in passing out, head pressure, severe headaches, slight head bobbing, feeling like I'm seeing in frames but i don't think there's a notable bounce in my eyes, eye pain, buzzing feeling in my head and throughout my body, brain fog/confusion, feeling like I'm zoning out all the time but can't bring myself back.  
I have had constant severe dizziness and vertigo and brain fog since I had COVID in mid-March. While I was sick with COVID, I had awful vertigo for about a week, then as I got better it subsided a bit, but never fully went away. I figured it would just take some time for my body to recover completely so I didn't think much of it. In late April, the vertigo got really bad again, and I felt a lot of pressure in my head and since I get sinus infections a lot I thought that was what was happening, so I went to urgent care. They said my ears were full of fluid and prescribed an antibiotic. After about 5 days I wasn't any better so I went to another urgent care and they said my ears were clear so I *should* be feeling better but changed the antibiotic because the previous one was giving me a lot of nausea. They also gave me prednisone in case there was inflammation. After a few weeks, the vertigo and dizziness let up a bit but again, never went away. I had tried taking meclizine, dramamine, Sudafed, Cetirizine, and a bunch of other OTC's for dizziness, allergies, and congestion but nothing helped. I went to my PCP in early May, and he said I needed to see an ENT but in the meantime should try vestibular therapy. I've been doing that for a few weeks but see absolutely no improvement. I saw my neurologist in early June, and brought this up to her. I had an MRI but everything came back normal. I also had a full metabolic label done, which was also normal. She told me an ENT should be able to help me because she didn't know what could be causing this. Last Tuesday, I was sent home from work because I was disoriented. I passed out when I got home. The vertigo has been very severe since then, I haven't gone to work or been able to do anything. Now I'm also experiencing a tingling feeling throughout my body, like a buzzing, not constantly but every once in a while. I went to the ENT today. They did some testing but could not give me any answers because there's no fluid, no obvious inflammation, the vertigo isn't brought on by posture changes, and my audio testing was normal. They're going to do more vestibular testing but that won't be for a few more weeks. I'm devastated. I've been sick for 4 months and nobody knows why. I can't keep missing work. I just started this job in April and I've missed weeks. Nothing helps. Please, please give me some thoughts, insight, advice, anything. I'm completely lost here and I don't know what to do. Thanks in advance.

Burning neck pain after Chiropractor— hEDS and fibromyalgia
AFAB, 27, weight 124, 5’3, BMI 21.97

hyper-mobility spectrum disorder, fibromyalgia

Depression, Autism, ADHD, OCD, Anxiety

Currently taking Bactirim for a UTI, and took Fluconazole for yeast infection, AZO for symptom relief, Wellbutrin 150 mg and Sertraline 100 mg tablets for depression and anxiety, adderall XR slow release capsules 10 mg for ADHD, iron tablets, 325 mg tabs, Meloxicam 15 mg for pain management related to hEDS and Fibro (as needed), hydroxyzine 50 mg tabs for anxiety (as needed), albuterol inhaler 108 mcg (as needed), vitamin D, probiotic, loratadine 10 mg for allergy, Tumeric Curcumim

 Despite apprehensions I have been going to a chiropractor, being convinced by my parents who had both had very good experiences and my twin (similar to my own info and including POTS) who also has. He is offering his service for free bc he knows my family so I felt this was less a money scam. He also apparently treats another girl with more severe EDS and she has said good things. My first visit I told him I was apprehensive and he seemed attentive and understanding. I was on the lookout for warning signs and he seemed to be the type to actually stay in his lane and focus on small adjustments. He also recommended PT. He took x-rays while I was in the room with him and able to see the screen, so he couldn’t make up a curve where there wasn’t one, and I knew I had mild scoliosis from a physical, so I was on the lookout for bullshit and didn’t find any. 

First visit he only did some very gentle “adjustments”, one that basically felt like a back massage and another to put my elbow back in place. He did a neck adjustment in that session and I didn’t think to mention I was against it until it happened. I didn’t want to be rude so I just saved it for next time. My neck seemed perfectly fine, however, so I was willing to give it another shot (I now know that the risk greatly outweighs any benefit). 

The second visit was much like the first (sans dislocation), until the neck adjustment. I IMMEDIATELY felt some discomfort, but thought it was from the movement. I did inform him that the last adjustments left me sore, but it wasn’t debilitating. This time, as I was leaving I began feeling a blooming pain all around my neck from the base of my head to just above the shoulders. I thought it was more soreness typical of this sort of thing— I feel sore after PT as well. But as time has gone one the pain hasn’t subsided at all, and actually increased a little. 

The back of my neck feels hot to the touch and there’s a burning pain sensation. I’m putting ice on it at the moment. I’m currently very worried that my choice to give the adjustments a second try has done serious damage, like vertebral artery dissection or http://thezebranetwork.org/craniocervical-instability <- craniocervical instability. Should I be preparing for worse developments and possible hospital visits or is this inflammation and my reminder to stick to my guns?

She and I both just have the sense that she isn't getting enough food/nutrients and she thinks it's not digesting well. Her stomach is always gurgling. She feels hungry but has no appetite. She is trying to drink Ensures.

Xifaxan (insurance wouldn't approve until she turned 18)

NAC  
Glutathione  
Prebiotics/Fiber  
ENT eval  
Sleep Study  
Starting meslamine again  
POTS test

I appreciate any suggestions.

Why is my (28F) alcohol tolerance lower after quitting SSRI's?
So I was on 150 mg bupropion hydrochloride and 50 mg sertraline for about 5 years for depression and anxiety. Recently with some major life changes (moving/working out more/new job/new relationship), I've essentially forgotten to take them so often that I kind of weaned myself off of them, and recently stopped taking them completely. Yes, I know this is not advised, but it genuinely happened without thinking. Previously, I've had severe withdrawals if I forgot them for 2 days, and suddenly I realized I hadn't taken them for over a week and a half, and felt totally normal, so I wanted to see how I function without them for a bit. Yes I've let my doctor know, and we're monitoring it.

My question is - while on them, I had an VERY high alcohol tolerance. (Yes, I know it's not advisable to drink while on them) With everything going on, I've barely drank - and now that I've completed quit taking them, I had a few drinks last night, and was surprised to see my tolerance is completely nonexistent now, uncomfortably so. I had about 3 drinks over the course of an evening, with food, and was absolutely hammered and went to bed by 8.30. 

I also noticed that despite having water, only a few drinks and food, the hangover this morning was like being hit with a truck. I never used to really get hangovers, and this one floored me.

Can someone explain why this might be?

Issues:

Ever since I quit smoking (100% tobacco/nicotine free as of 6 years ago), I've been struggling with what I can only describe as chronic, systemic swelling issues -- joint pain/swelling, bloating, occasional bouts of nausea and fuzzy-headedness. I get sick (colds, flus, sinus infections, stomach bugs) at least once a month. I have been losing weight (was 270 lbs) and started Tirzepatide ~7 months ago, but I've been stalled at ~240 lbs for ~four months. The frequency of my insomnia and illness made exercise routines difficult to maintain.

Whenever I do any kind of exercise, even though I don't feel tired and don't push myself (not out of breath, not tired), my body's reaction is like an allergic reaction. If I do 1 mile over a 1/2 an hour at minimal incline on the treadmill for 2-3 times over 3-4 days, I come down with something. If I go on a light two mile hike (keeping pace with my 4 year old, lightly sloping trails, which my wife, 8 and 4 year-olds have no trouble with), I spend the next 3-4 days with extreme soreness and then come down with something. 

Last Tuesday, we went on a trivial 2 mile hike, it was cool, I was hydrated, had a decent breakfast and a reasonable dinner the night before, we stopped frequently, but the next day my legs were extremely sore and the day after that I came down with a cold that has lingered since. No one else was sore or got sick despite us all being in close proximity. The soreness is not quite debilitating but much closer to debilitating than mere soreness. The sickness started two days later with cold/flu like symptoms, moodiness, feeling run down, exhaustion, mild sinus and throat symptoms, and so on.

All of my weight is in my gut. Despite the above, I retain muscle development in my calves, chest, shoulders, and arms from when I was more active. I suffer from near-constant back pain, but I do not experience weakness or lack of coordination - I can pick up heavy weights and am not afraid of dropping things. That said, I've had signs of arthritis since I was in my late teens -- pain and swelling in joints.

I have done rounds with doctors checking my bloodwork, hormones, allergies, etc., and they all insist that other than cholesterol, I'm a brick house for my age. And yet I feel like shit all the time. And over the past 6 weeks I have had bouts of stomach flu (nausea, diarrhea, etc.) lasting initially 5 days, then 3, now 24-48 hours, every week or other week.

I ascribed everything to weight, focused on the Tirzepatide, but here I am after 7 months on that medication and 1.5 years after my last round of banging on various doctor's doors.

We moved from north-central FL to northwest GA in 2021 and nothing has changed, so I don't believe it's environmental. 

The first time I quit smoking for 6 months in early 2015, I was hitting the gym for hours at a time, pushing myself more than I did when I was a teenager, and had none of these issues.

Thank you for any insight you can share.
