Hi! Here are some things to know about me:   
Age: 21  
Sex: Female  
Height: 5'7"  
Weight: 260lbs  
Medications being taken: 

* Nikki (BC) 3mg - Started taking in November to help regulate cycles, will explain what led to this down below
* 50mg Sertraline - Started in August, there was a period from December to January where I couldn't get it due to a miscommunication between pharmacies but since then I have been able to be more consistent in taking it
* 300 mg buPROPion - same as the sertraline 

This is a very long story, I will do my best to break it out into paragraphs, I worry it could all be connected and I don't want to leave a stone unturned.   


Back in high school I was around 170 and regularly playing sports. By the end of high school I was at 200lbs and feel that was due to bodily changes and no longer playing active sports.  When I got to college that moved up to 220lbs, I feel in large part due to Covid and it being freshman year. I started focusing on portions, still eating things I enjoyed but being more mindful and was able to drop some weight. But it's always been a problem for me, I struggle with textures, smells, looks of food and I've been trying to work through it.   


I have had a very stressful college experience, after my Sophomore (2021/2022) year I went to my doctor's with my concerns and was given Prozac. I was also able to get accommodations for testing anxiety. This definitely helped and I worked on trying to manage my anxieties through a school therapist. I never felt like the medicine did anything but just kept taking it. 

Going into November 2022 I was at 220lbs. Before this time, I had a period every, single month, a 30 day cycle. the only time it would very would be around finals week at the end of each semester which I contributed to stress. Going into December of 2022 I realized I had gained what felt like a significant amount of weight, so I purchased a scale. In January 2023 I was 250lbs. Also in November/December of 2022 was when my periods would start to vary more. I would only have a period every other month and on the months I did not bleed, I would still feel very yuck and crampy. Instead of my cycle being 30-35 days it became 58-60 days.    


I started to get concerned, and went to the doctor because while I had still been eating foods I liked (admittedly not healthy foods) I was using a food tracker to try and watch portions, I cut out sugary drinks, rarely snacked, and ate two meals a day, never full on pigging out and stopping before I was full. However I did acknowledge this was a potential reason for the period and weight concerns. I still decided to get it checked out after taking a physiology class that raised some concerns.   


At this point we are in March 2023 and at first I went to a student health doctor on my campus. They did blood work, and ran CMP, Vitamin D, CBC, Glucose and TSH labs. The only things slightly low was my Vitamin D level (19.4 ng/ml) and then my liver enzymes were slightly elevated (AST of 43u/L and ALT of 50 u/L). The doctor suggested Weight Watches and to walk more. They told me my cycle was normal and they had met plenty of people who had cycles that long.   


I tried my best to focus even more on trying healthier foods, continuing to not snack or drink sugary drinks, etc. I still had concerns though and in May 2023 I went to see my PCP. My PCP ran the same labs again, I was at 256lbs. They also ran lipid, Testosterone, LH, and FSH panels alongside the CBC and CMP. Everything was normal again except for the CMP where I had elevated liver enzymes again (AST was 50 u/L and ALT was 52 u/L). They told me to stop taking NSAIDs and to not drink alcohol (which was not something I commonly did). They did the CMP again a week later, the labs were still elevated but slightly less (AST was 41 and ALT was 47). They then tested me for Hepatitis and did an abdominal ultrasound. The Hepatitis came back negative. The result from this was mild fatty liver which they told me wasn't a huge deal.   


At this point I felt they weren't listening to my cycle concerns and I pushed to be seen by a gynecologist since I was almost 21 and needed to get a Pap smear. They did not want to refer me since I wasn't 21 but I turned 21 in June so they finally agreed. I was able to get once scheduled for September 2023.   


I went from April to mid-July without a period and felt miserable and just off the whole time. In early July I started to spot and spotted from July 10th all the way to fully starting on July 25th. I spent the summer doing walking, and still trying to manage healthier eating and portions while also battling food aversions.  I went to the gynecologist in September where I had an awful experience. The doctor joked about my weight a lot and it was bad so I went back to student health in October and they were able to do a Pap smear and it was all good. The doctor encouraged birth control, which I went on in November and that has helped to regulate my periods. Also all through this time I was fluctuating between 245-250, I swear I've really been trying. I also went to the behavioral health center on campus where they switched me to a wellbutrin/sertraline combo which has, I feel, been able to really help me manage my anxiety and depression.   


Since then:   
I have started having more digestive type issues since January. I've had almost constant acid reflux for over a year. I tried one of those two week courses of medicine you can find on the shelf to help but it didn't at all. I turned 21 in June, I've tried maybe 6 drinks in that time frame (it's March now) and I hate the taste and it makes me feel yuck and nauseous even after just 1 so I don't drink.   
In the past month I have been having times where I wake up 5-6 hours after eating with intense mid to upper stomach and back pain it was like a band of pain that wrapped around my body. It's like a 8/10 on the pain scale.  I thought it was heartburn or indigestion so I would try a Pepto, warm shower, nothing would help. I would be up for hours in tears. Before it somewhat subside and I would feel a little better. The last one happened on 3/12 into 3/13. 

 I feel nauseous way more than I ever used to, after eating or while in the car. Also in the past week my bathroom activities have been a lot more different. It used to be, I would have a regular poop once a day, of the firm but not too firm consistency you would expect and normal color unless I ate like something green or blue. I feel like every time I sit on the toilet now (3-5 times a day at least) I poop. It's not completely runny but it's not firm in the slightest. It's also had the strangest, weirdest odor. I have no idea what to explain it like but it's different and worse than normal. It's also become a lot darker. I don't know if it's really a black, I can't really tell but it's definitely a super dark brown at the least. I have just felt off lately. I haven't eaten anything super fiber containing, the last time I had Pepto was on the 13th.   


I feel like it all probably relates to my weight. It's something I've struggled with and have tried to work on it. I haven't changed my diet in terms of types of food since I was at 200lbs in high school and I've focused on portions and more activity. I feel like maybe I should get it checked out? But I also feel like maybe it isn't worth it and I need to just try harder to lose weight. I was hoping for some insight on what to do. I apologize if this is still jumbled sounding, I'm becoming more concerned since the digestive issues started occurring but I don't want to go if it's highly likely I'm going to be told to lose weight since that is something I've been working at.

Can substances induce week-long "psychoses"? My experience

Preface: I've had problems of light depression for years, on and off, very rarely I've had anxiety, I've never had a panic attack. TW: drugs, anxiety

My experience of almost three years ago: I was going through a rough time sentimentally and was overall in a bad place. On NYE I mixed a slightly higher than "usual" amount of substances that definitely shouldn't be mixed - alcohol, cocaine and MDMA all together, not in huge quantities but I'm very small, Idk. My body immediately had a strong reaction - threw up, couldn't sleep, then for a couple of days I was fine. Then the most HORRIFIC experience of my life started and lasted for around 40-50 days. I stopped sleeping. I experienced HUGE anxiety every second that I was awake, paranoia, super intrusive thoughts, my stomach was completely shut and I lost 4 kg in 2 weeks. I was still "myself" and could kinda function socially but it required every ounce of my strength and will. I was kind of frozen in panic, from what I've read about panic attacks they're different: this felt acute just ALL the time, imagine someone making a prank on you and you JUMP in scare. This feeling, this state of sudden and brief panic, but ongoing for longer than a month. I felt like I had no walls to protect my subconscious, I had horrific nightmares which literally felt REAL, I was deeply depressed and thinking I could never be happy again. I showered twice in a month because I couldn't be alone in a room, I was super scared of being alone in a room. I moved to a friend's house and she took care of me. She cooked and did everything that I needed, I was restless, I couldn't watch a movie or read a book or watch the news or anything because they gave me strong anxiety and I thought I would just go crazy. I experienced STRONG depersonalization and that was the most horrible thing I've ever felt.

I started taking benzodiazepines and a light dose (50 mg) of antidepressants (sertraline) and they worked very well, in around a month the anxiety stopped and I could sleep and live again.

I'm SURE that all this was due to the drug use, BUT my therapist/psychiatrist says that the chemical residue of drugs disappears from the brain in a couple of days, they're just not there anymore. So it must have been "me" or "my brain" making all this mess, not the drugs. I can't reconcile this idea with the brutality of this experience (my brain did this without drugs?) and Im scared it might happen again even w/o substances.

is it your experience too or your medical opinion that substances can unclench even week-long "psychoses"? I don't know what to make of this. Does anyone have an explanation?

Patient: M20, 178 cm, 83 kg

History: hay fever, essential tremor, borderline personality disorder, unspecified mood disorder, recent COVID-19

Medication: daily sertraline 100 mg, lamotrigine 100 mg, aripiprazole 15 mg, atorvastatin 10 mg, vitamin D 5000 IU; mexidol 100 mg IM; recently, armodafinil 150 mg

Symptoms: hypersomnia (don't feel rested after 10-12 hours of sleep), low productivity, low mood, feeling of hopelessness. Happens periodically, but was attributed to atypical depression, Current onset several months ago, got worse after the COVID-19 infection.

Lab tests: hemoglobin, free T4, TSH, and vitamin D within range. EEG with some non-epileptic abnormalities, brain MRI clean — several years ago.

The main question is: what specialist should I see first, and whether I should do some tests before the appointment. I don't have a bunch of money, and doctors are expensive in my country, so I want to go to the right one with all the needed blood work and tests first try. 

My thoughts as a biologist but not a doctor on my condition are:

1 Treatment-resistant atypical depression

Already on SSRIs, no loss of interest in things that bring me joy, no other signs of atypical form.

2 Bipolar depression

Again, no loss of interest, no previous hypomanic episodes? But I guess I had mixed one. Got response to lamotrigine for similar symptoms in the past. Should I ask my psychiatrist for bipolar disorder evaluation?

3 Idiopathic hypersomnia

Explains all the symptoms but I don't have symptoms every day but periodically.

4 Sleep apnea

Sleep is long without waking up in the middle of the night.

4 post-COVID syndrome

The symptoms were before the infection but weren't so severe. In that case, is there's something one may do?

So, should I see a psychiatrist or a neurologist first? Maybe I should do a polysomnography before visiting a neurologist?

Thank you!

Antidepressants is making me more depressed?
Age: 19
Sex: Male
Height: 180
Weight: 55

I've been taking antidepressants since June 2022. Fluoxetine (20 mg) and Olanzapine (2.5 mg) were the first meds prescribed to me by my doctor. 

First 20 days were like hell to me and then I felt good for 3 days and boom that feeling is gone and got more depressed.

2 months passed like that and on August I was on the edge and attempted suicide for the first time in my life family took me to ER and stayed there for two days and I was released.

After that my doctor changed my meds to Sertraline (200 mg) Risperidone (3 mg) Xanax (1 mg) Xanax helped me a lot with anxiety and panic attacks and Risperidone helped me with sleeping and having less hallucination but Sertraline didn't help with depression at all. 

In November I changed my doctor and hospital and I wasn't able to take it anymore and I was more suicidal than before so my doctor suggested that I should be in thier rehab at hospital (that's how it works here every hospital has a rehab) I stayed in rehab for a month and half they changed my meds to Venlafaxine (150 mg) Quetiapine (300 mg) Xanax (1 mg) for me these meds didn't help like the ones before..totally the opposite I got more depressed. 

On the new year I decided to get off meds and start a new page because I'm sick of it but unfortunately I didn't expect that's the worst idea. 

First two weeks were like hell I didn't want to go to work I didn't want to wake up I didn't want to do anything started to drink and smoke a lot. 

At the end I couldn't take it again and visited my doctor and prescribed me Fluoxetine again. 

It's been two weeks since I'm back to taking meds again and it still feels like I'm off meds. 

I've never been depressed like this before and I'm even more suicidal. What I can do next? Get to rehab again? Change my meds? 

I remember the days before deciding taking antidepressants...yes I was depressed but if knew these meds gonna have a long term effects like this I wouldn't take it and I wish I didn't.

Weeks of abdominal pain
19 FTM, 5’6”, 124 lbs. I have a history of anxiety and depression, I take 100 mg sertraline daily and 60 mg testosterone weekly (started just over three years ago, I have not experienced menstrual cycles in over two years). I also use edibles a couple times a week to help with sleep. I have eosinophilic esophagitis, the only trigger that I know of is dairy.

I developed some pain in my lower right abdomen around November 5th or 6th, which got slightly worse within ~10 minutes of eating. Over the course of a couple weeks, this pain got worse, and continued to flare up significantly after eating. Around Nov 14th, the pain started to radiate through my lower back and down my right leg, and as it flared up I became lightheaded and shaky. At the start of November, I was 140 lbs, and have lost around 16 lbs because eating causes me so much pain. On Nov 21st, I was in enough pain and so lightheaded that I went to the ER (out of my home state).

At the ER I received a CT scan, and fluid was seen near my right ovary. I was told I had a ruptured ovarian cyst, and to take ibuprofen and expect improvement soon. I went to my primary care doc on Nov 25th when I was back in my home state and she was unable to offer further advice. 

On Nov 26th, the pain was getting worse so I went to the ER again and received an ultrasound, blood work, and a second CT scan. The ultrasound showed only a very small amount of fluid, which was near my appendix. My appendix was a normal size, and my kidneys looked normal. My blood work showed elevated eosinophils and a somewhat low anion gap. My abdomen is very sensitive to pressure, which concerned the doctor enough to order a second CT scan, but it didn’t find anything. The doctors at this ER didn’t believe the problem was a ruptured cyst, given the duration of pain and the extremely small amount of fluid, but they weren’t able to provide further answers.

At this point, the scans and blood work have ruled out cancer/tumors, appendicitis, kidney stones, celiac, and intestinal blockages. I’m at a loss, I’ll be seeing a GI specialist as soon as I can but thought I might as well ask if anyone knows what this could be.

High heart rate for a little over a month?
30F 
Recently started sertraline
Propranolol as needed (for anxiety)
Copper IUD

In August I was dealing with very dry eyes/nose and it caused sleep issues. Kept waking up with anxiety/high heart rate. 

Dr prescribed 3 antihistamines (fexofenadine, hydroxyzine, and nasal steroid) thinking it was allergies. It ended up not being allergies (got tested). Best guess is dry eye. I ended up having a paradoxical reaction to antihistamines (extreme agitation/anxiety, profuse sweating and tremors. Woke up to extreme adrenaline surges and absolute panic attacks). Was on them for a week and then stopped them. I mentally spiraled and then my sleep issues got worse for a couple weeks or so. Had to be on trazadone to force myself to sleep. My heart rate would stay at 100 -120bpm all day and while I was trying to sleep. The insomnia definitely made my heart rate and anxiety worse. Things got better but my high heart rate lasted for a little over a month and the last two weeks my sleep and heart rate have finally gone back to normal (when relaxed 58-65bpm)

It seems weird to blame the anti histamines since I had these issues for 3-4 weeks after stopping the medicine. I also had some of the issues before when experiencing the dry eye. So Dr blood tested thyroid (normal) and 24 hour urine hormone test (normal). She now thinks it's anxiety caused (I do have an anxiety disorder but this is so abnormal for me). So she put me on sertraline (started a week ago, 12.5 mg working up to 25mg). There's no way the sertraline could kick in this fast (heart rate has improved last week as well). EKGs have come back normal, and I had a recent ultrasound on my heart as I had experienced isolated chest pains one day (and the ultrasound came back okay)

What the heck is going on? I feel like anxiety has been the effect of these symptoms and not the cause. Should I be switching primary care providers? I'm concerned that there's issues with my heart sinus rhythm or maybe this was some post viral fatigue issues that the antihistamines sent me in a full spiral? Right now she wants to continue just seeing if things stay normal/if sertraline helps. 

I have a sleep study lined up but the sleep DR does not think this is sleep apnea and also suggested anxiety. My primary care said an holter monitor seemed over kill but it was up to me if I wanted to wear one? 

I guess what I'm asking is, is this actually likely anxiety? Or should I be switching primary care Drs or requesting specific tests to be done? Ive been feeling good the last two weeks but I find it unnerving how bad this got.

Hip Labral Tear Advice - Surgery or no surgery?
Hey everyone, I am a 32F caucasian Australian. I do not drink, smoke, or take recreational drugs. I am currently on 100 mg sertraline for depression. I am 155cms tall and 55kgs. I have had two children, both via C-Section. 

I was unfortunately involved in a car accident just over a month ago where a car was going approx. 80km/h when they hit me in the rear, pushing me into the car in front. 

When I got out of the car, I immediately felt pain down the right side of my leg and was limping around while organising the tow trucks to take all three of our cars off the motorway. Anyway, I went home, and my partner took me to see a doctor who told me it wasn't a serious crash because the airbags did not go off and I should go home and take some ibuprofen. My partner told the doctor that I was in a lot of pain so could we get some scans done or some further examination to make sure everything was okay. This doctor then asked me if I wanted an xray and if I did, where did I want the xray. I indicated I wanted it done on my right hip and leg area as that was where I was feeling pain, and also on my back because I was feeling the effects of whiplash. 

My results came back the next day, and I decided to see a different, more compassionate doctor. He told me the scans showed I had a degenerative disease, and he stated it was likely osteoarthritis which was causing the pain, which was weird because I had not felt pain in that area previously. He then ordered a CT scan to see the extent of the arthritis. I got the scan done and about two hours later, the doctor said I needed to go to hospital immediately as it appeared I had a fractured femur. I rushed myself to the emergency department of my local hospital where I was given another xray which was inconclusive and I was told to follow up the next week with an orthopaedic surgeon, and to also get another CT scan. 

I got the CT scan done and saw the orthopaedic surgeon who did not really provide me with any advice on what the issue could be, but told me to get an MRI and then come back to see him. I got the MRI done and finally had my answer. I have a anterosuperior labral tear of the hip which is why I am in the pain I am in. He has advised me to seek out physiotherapy, to weight bare as tolerated and to see him in two months. I asked him if I needed surgery and he said no I do not, it would do more harm than good. He did not mention anything about the arthritis and at this point I have no idea whether it was a misdiagnosis, or whether I do have arthritis.

As all humans do, I went down a Google rabbit hole and read blog posts, forums, and peer reviewed journal articles about labral tears, what they are, the treatments for them, and the majority say that while physiotherapy can help to reduce the pain, it cannot fix the tear, and the tear can become worse without surgery. It also said labral tears can lead the patient to being at more risk of needing a hip replacement in the future. 

My question is, should I be pushing for surgery? I understand there are risks involved with all surgeries. However, I am worried that if I leave the tear it is just going to get worse, even with physiotherapy, and I should get the surgery while I am young and can bounce back better, rather than doing physiotherapy, and then needing the surgery anyway, and then completing more physiotherapy. 

Currently my pain level is at the point where I am resting most of the day and I only find comfort when laying down. I try not to take anti-inflamatories too often as I know that it isn't good for me to be on them long term. I am an office worker and am worried that when I go back to work, I will end up in pain for most of the day as sitting down aggravates the symptoms, and I can only stand for maybe five minutes at a time. I also cannot run around with my kids who are 5 and 3 and little balls of energy. This has greatly affected my life and I am wanting to get back to some normalcy. I know I probably will never get back to how I was before the accident, and surgery won't be a magical cure, but I just cant bare the thought of not getting the surgery, and then things getting worse.

Can’t do this anymore

It all began back in Oct 2020. I was 19 and had just started university and was struggling quite a lot feeling anxious. I drank more than I should and was unwell for a period with gastroenteritis. I’d already been to A&E in pain and they told me I should recover in a couple of weeks with drinking lots of fluids and looking after myself. Shortly after this I woke up one day with loss of sensation in the right side of my face, and strange vision in my right side. I felt really confused and distressed and wasn’t sure what was happening and decided to return home. I was really unwell, my mum refused to let me go to the hospital again and determined I was just in a state of psychological distress. I spoke to a doctor over the phone who resolved it was a  combination of migraine, gastroenteritis and anxiety. They also prescribed me Sertraline which I had been on before. The numbness and vision issues only lasted a day or so but I felt really fatigued and had aches and pains for about a week. However, I made a good recovery at home and found a job following this. I was ok for a while until March 2021 when I started experiencing heart palpitations and tightness in my chest. I talked to a GP again who resolved it was either heartburn or anxiety but sent me for blood tests which came back normal. I began to think back to what happened, Googling my symptoms, worrying I had a stroke, atrial fibrillation or some kind of nerve damage. The heart palpitations became more frequent around May 2021 and I began to get painful tingling sensations and numbness in the right side of my face which spread down one side of my body. I was really concerned and managed to get an in person appointment with a different doctor. He examined me, couldn’t find anything visibly wrong but was concerned and sent me for lots more tests. I had a few ECGs, echocardiogram, blood tests, 24 hour Holter Monitor, an MRI and a contrast MRI. I was also seen by a neurologist. All the tests came back normal and clear. My doctor said he could rule out possibility of a stroke or heart problems. I was referred to mental health services and was diagnosed with conversion disorder/ somatic symptoms. The symptoms continued throughout the summer despite being on medication. I felt like there was something physically/ neurologically wrong that the tests had missed. Finally the symptoms began to subside in August 2021. I had a fresh start at university in September and I decided to put it all behind me and to try and live a healthy lifestyle. However, in the back of my mind it still felt like there was something wrong. I had stiffer and clickier joints, some back pain and neck pain and it always felt like one side of my body was weaker. I also have problems concentrating and have ‘brain fog’ and never feel truly rested after sleep. I tried to ignore this and did swimming, yoga and meditation and continued living my life. I also started weekly therapy. However in the past couple of weeks the numbness and heart palpitations have returned. I am in a lot of discomfort and pain and distress. I have honestly given up going down a medical route and just feel hopeless. I’m only 21 and I don’t want to keep living like this. I don’t know what to do anymore if the symptoms continue. 

 Just felt like I needed to rant and share my story. If you have any advice for me it would be greatly appreciated.

Hello all, just joined this group earlier today. My story is complicated, and I've had to tell it alongside giving my medical records to my PCP, cardiologist, neurologist, physiatrist, physical therapist, and pain specialist and I feel like my pain physician (who is an NP, not an MD) still doesn't understand the extent of my pain, though she has tried.

Short story: October 11, 2016 I suffered a near death experience that left me disabled and in fairly constant pain with lightning bolts of sharp pain at seemingly random intervals. 

Longer story: I experienced a simultaneous spontaneous (no aneurysm prior) type A and B ascending and descending AORTIC DISSECTION from the arch all the way down to my iliac artery. This cut off blood circulation to my left leg and my kidneys for about 12 hours until it was repaired. Essentially I experienced compartment syndrome in my left leg and it swelled up like a balloon. After my aorta was repaired, 2 fasciotomies were made on either side of my calf muscle to relieve pressure on my lower leg and foot to attempt to delay nerve death until the swelling could be dealt with. I was in the hospital on dialysis for weeks until my kidneys kicked back in, long term care, and inpatient physical therapy for a total of 80 days. When wound care had to change dressings on my leg fasciotomy open wounds (had to have skin grafts, skin taken from my upper leg) they had to put me on Dilaudid, it caused so much pain. My blood pressure would shoot up so high from the pain the docs were afraid I'd pop a stitch on the aortic arch graft without major temporary pain relief. It helped.

After hospitalization, I was initially in a wheelchair, then with constant physical therapy I graduated to a KAFO leg brace and then an AFO ankle brace about 2 years later, which I'm still using while walking with a cane. Permanently, I've got very little sensation or mobility in my lower left leg, especially my ankle. I've also got a mandate from a slew of doctors telling me I can't ever go on roller coasters, scuba dive, lift anything over 40 pounds, or even hold my breath for any real length of time for fear of pressure on the Dacron arch graft causing it to pull away, which would result in my bleeding out internally in a matter of seconds.

So with nerve death and damage I've got constant burning pain with random sharp intense stabs (I call them lightning bolts) that I am treating. Along with back and knee pain from not having a natural walking gait anymore, which is steadily increasing as physical therapy and my neurologist tell me my leg is as good as it's going to get. 

I've been diagnosed with a vascular version of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS), a connective tissue disorder, hence the aortic dissection with no warning, severe neuropathy, along with CRPS in the lower left leg/foot, a couple herniated disks from walking and standing crookedly and PTSD from the horrible near death experience. I've got skin grafted scars on my left calf that are frightening to young children and a zipper scar and permanent dent in my breastbone from emergency open heart surgery. A Dacron aortic arch graft and 5 stents holding the rest of my aorta in place are my cyborg parts and with all the scars I feel like some kind of messed up prototype Terminator who only wants to terminate himself on bad days.

I'm in physical therapy twice a week now to help manage pain. I take Lyrica but hate it because it makes me puff up, and it does nothing for the back pain and the constant tingling burning pain, just reduces the lightning bolts. Prior to Lyrica,I tried gabapentin and had little relief, then low doses of amitriptyline and sertraline (antidepressant/ anti anxiety meds) that worked only slightly better. 

After treating my pain for 3 years, my neurologist sent me to a pain clinic when he said he would no longer help manage my opioid meds, but he is still managing my antidepressants. I also take a handful of hypertension meds to make sure my BP stays low, and my Percs, which have proven to be the only thing that mutes all pain to the point where I can concentrate for work, play with my kids, and function in general.

At the pain clinic I've had lidocaine trigger point injections (little to no effect on back pain, nothing for neuropathic pain), radio frequency ablation (some back pain relief, which returned after about 3 months, little to no effect on neuropathic pain), and a continuance of my opioid prescription. We are looking into nerve block injections in the back next, and SCS as an absolute last resort.

Problem is, I've been on the same dosage of opioid pain relief food going on 4 years now, since my neurologist passed me off as his pain patient to the pain clinic. More and more I'm not getting as much relief from the Oxy, or it doesn't last as long. They're not keen on increasing my dosage or trying to change meds for some reason, but now I'm having to endure more pain during the day in order to be able to have enough relief to sleep at night. I know my body has built up a tolerance since I've been on the same 40mg/day for years now, but how do I make it as effective as it once was? Failing that, any tips for helping my pain physician understand that the vast majority of my relief covers from these pills and they aren't working as well as they used to?

Sorry for the long story but I've got nobody to tell it to who will listen. I'm lucky to be alive, and I appreciate that fact, but my quality of that life is dwindling, and I'm afraid at some point I'll start thinking seriously otherwise. Thanks for reading.

Posting on behalf of my little brother -- Chronic leg/back/achilles pain
*Hi there,*

*My 28 year old brother is coming up on 2 years with chronic pain, mostly in his leg. He is riddled with anxiety and depression because of it, and is too nervous to post here for fearing of hearing the worst. No doctor can seem to tell him what's wrong, as the MRIs come back pretty clean (thank god). But he's really just looking for an answer. A diagnosis. Some relief. I told him he needs a support group but again, he's afraid of what he might hear.*

*I asked if I could post on his behalf, to act as a filter for replies. Here is his story:*

In June 2019, I woke up with pain around my right knee. A month later the pain was so bad I couldn’t walk for a night. Never happened like that again. Pain continued. Received Xray and MRI (practically clean), **diagnosed as** **patellafemoral pain syndrome / IT band syndrome.** Did physically therapy on knee for 4 months. Pain gradually started to moved up the leg on the outside and below the knee a bit. **Pain never went away.** I have somewhat pins and needles sensation, like a blanket over the side of my front shin.

7 months in, bad back pain started to happen, received MRI of my back which showed mild bulging discs on several lumbar discs (mainly L4/L5): **diagnosed as lumbar radiculopathy.** I was told walking was ok so I would walk around the neighborhood a lot with hills. Ended up developing a small string of pain at the bottom of my heel (what felt like the start of insertional achilles tendonitis). When I’d point my toes towards my face, I would feel that pull at the bottom of my heel. Two months into seeing a chiropractor and biking this went away. At this time, driving was my worst friend, it was super painful to sit in car. My low back and even a little further up would be so painful. The car also gives me problems now mostly at the top of the outside thigh and sometimes above knee on the outside. For the thigh, it’s almost like a 7 inch line along the femur.

Began biking every other day or so for an hour. Loved it. Didn’t have a lot of pain biking but afterwards would feel it in the leg. In the fall of 2020 I started to feel the heel thing again but it was hiding a bit. This whole time I figure I'll just have nerve pain that won’t go away for god knows how long. My achilles pain start to ramp up in early 2021 and the whole back of my heel was painful. I went to Physical Therapy for insertional and non insertional achilles tendonitis.

After a month of not much improvement, I got an MRI on my foot. Showed practically nothing. Received knew MRI of my back and saw an amazing doctor in Philadelphia. New MRI showed mild bulging discs on L2-L3, L3-L4, L4-L5 (with a left foramina disc protrusion which contacts the adjacent nerve root. Mild left subarticular recess stenosis. No significant central canal or foramina narrowing. **The thing is, I have pain down the right leg, not the left.** The surgeon said I will never need back surgery and to see a Neurologist again (for the leg pain) and Physiatrist (to help with chronic back pain).

**What I've tried:**

* Physically therapy for 3 months. Felt ok but No change.
* 2 Nerve root block shots, No Change.
* Chiropractor for 4 months. Felt good in the beginning but No Change.
* ART therapy for 5 sessions. No change.
* Acupuncture 7 sessions - No change.
* Saw a Neurologist - EMG came out fine.
* Blood tests at end of 2019 shows no sign of limes disease, or rheumatoid arthritis.

​

**What makes me feel better?**

* Exercise, in the moment, (when the achilles isn’t hurting). The leg may start to develop some pain.
* Heating pad on low back generally feels good.
* CBD capsules/ tincture I can dig (helps the mental aspect, not really the pain?)
* Standing more often than sitting is always preferred. Love my standing desk!

Am interested in seeing if Gabapentin would effect me - I just started 25mg Sertraline for anxiety last week so I need to let that settle in first.

Taking Advil or Tylenol doesn’t help the nerve pain down the leg.

Still haven’t taken a caudal steroid shot that was offered to me that hits more of a general area in low back. I am interested in trying this.

*Can anyone offer any words of wisdom? Ideas on what it may be? Thank you.*

Getting treated for anxiety and depression, but sexual dysfunction and general unhappiness persists, how long should it take to get better?
I am being treated for generalised anxiety disorder and associated depression with Sertraline 200mg. Along with that for weight-loss(from Sertraline) I am having Contrave(naltrexone+bupropion) and vilazodone 20mg. My psych started vilazodone with Contrave because his clinical experience suggested that for my condition, contrave may cause depression or low mood. Anxiety wise I am doing okay. But I still have irritability, social anxiety, etc. Also, I am neither happy nor excited about anything in life at the moment. 

Now when I look back I realise I was a low-key anxious person since childhood. Going somewhere (grocery, movies, etc) alone was never an option. Either someone should accompany me or I should speak someone on the phone. This is me 17 years old. Now I am 31yrs. 

I have had sexual desire and relationships during my teen years. But, I, lost interest in sexual things like attraction, making out etc a few years back. I was not officially detected with GAD or depression then, yet. I am talking about the desire part, the first part in the process. I stopped craving or wanting it. 

Then 2022 I started seeing a therapist. She started seeing my problems and ultimately suggested I try medication. I ran away. Then after one of my friends died and my depression became worse and I decided to start meds from November 2023. My psych gradually upped me to 200mg. My anxiety is gone in a way that I don't get panic attacks anymore. But the irritation I got from anything sexual has turned into apathy. 

Also I lost motivation. So my psych tried me on Modafinil which only made me a robot. Topiramate for weight loss made me angry like a fireball. Now I am on 200mg Sertraline, 20mg Vilazodone and full dose Contrave. Contrave has started working and I lost 8 kgs in 4 months. 

But, I haven't had any change in life moment with these medications yet. I don't get excited or happy to do anything or anticipate anything other than my work (which makes me irritable quite often). I still don't have sexual desire. By desire I mean the mental wanting part, not that I can't orgasm etc. I am also not responding to touch or any signs of mental or physical intimacy. Is this my depression or something else. I feel irritated at small things sometimes, but, it is much much less than before. Also the anger and rage has reduced much but still happens sometimes.

All I am asking, is this normal? I know emotional blunting happens with SSRIs. I haven't specifically told my psych about the loss of sexual desire (I am still uncomfortable at this stage) but I have shared my concern about not feeling excited about any aspect of life. I don't seek any activity that may secrete happy chemicals in my body. My psych says it will get better one thing at a time.

At this point, though I feel that outright fixing only my sexual dysfunction won't do any good as I am not happy in other aspects of life too. I want to be a overall happy and excited with life individual.

Since it has been exactly 1 year since I started treatment, am I expecting things to happen too fast? Does it take longer e.g. depression takes longer to lift than anxiety or the reverse?

Anyone with any knowledge about this kindly share your thoughts.

Anyone taking more than 200mg of Sertraline for treating their anxiety and associated depression?

Is this normal? Or should have my psych got me started on a new medication and gradually tapered off Sertraline.

P.S: I have no major side effects other than what I described.

(long story). she tried to make the marriage work however but was met with extreme physical, mental and verbal torment, including over 10 attempts of him trying to kill her, in which she escaped all. She moved away after 7 years of enduring this (didn't move sooner due to family traditions, no money, no family, not much education). But it left her with irreparable damage mentally. We haven't seen him in over 18 years and yet she speaks of him daily, not even realising the extent of her trauma. Everything I do and say, if negative, triggers a thought and she is instantly reminded of something similar he did, which she tells me in the form 'you're being just like your father' - a man who's face I don't even remember, who's voice I do not care for. My mother is kind and caring but she has moments where she lashes out for no reason, I know this is due to her triggers - which I have tried to talk to her about and get her into therapy but she says it is for people with no backbone.

She works as a nurse and for the past 3/4 years has been having trouble with the other nurses and workers there. The patients always all adore her, and she them, she loves to care for people. However the nurses who like doing the bare minimum (majority of the NHS) don't like the comparison I suppose. She has been getting severely bullied by nurses in several wards, despite moving. To the point of them grouping against her and LYING about her doing things very wrong to get her pin taken off her and get her fired. She was diagnosed with depression 3 years ago but doesn't take sertraline for it as it makes her numb. She now has chronic stress and constant high blood pressure and headaches. She also has suicidal thoughts (I read some of her diary). It said that if she didn't have to look after me, she would have offed herself by now....

And there is nothing I can do. I wanted to get a second job on the side of my part time one as I'm in college but she said no as I need to focus on my studies. But I can't continue seeing her suffer. I just want to get a big job so I can pay for the house and everything so she doesn't have to work anymore. I can't even concentrate on my studies, I just distract myself from my mum and everything by doing meaningless things like scrolling on my phone and shutting myself in my room, coming home late after walking around the mall for ages just thinking and listening to music. My grades are suffering because of this too. I feel like a failure and that I should have solved this problem by now and retired her at her age. If she keeps going to her job she will keep paying with her mental health until there is nothing left. I feel like I can't even speak to her anymore, she's constantly zoning out, deep in thought, never really there when I speak to her. I feel like she's going right before my eyes. I have nobody else. I feel so sick knowing I could be doing something to help her but I can't.

I don't know what to do anymore.

Health anxiety is back with a bang!!
I (29, F) have HEALTH ANXIETY again. I thought I’d tamed it, but I was wrong.

Background: Childhood trauma—abuse, neglect, drug-addicted parents. Mum died when I was 26, leading to my first experience with SSRIs (sertraline) for depression and anxiety. It helped for a while but left me numb and caused weight gain. I stopped taking it to feel something again.

In 2019, I had my first PANIC ATTACK on a flight home. A nurse thought I was having a heart attack, but it was Costochondritis (chest wall inflammation mimicking heart attack symptoms). It was painful, and I didn’t believe I wasn’t dying. This kicked off health anxiety. Every breath felt like my last; every part of my body felt wrong for months. I started on Lexapro, which took a month of hell to kick in but worked. I healed my chest through exercise and physio, gained weight, but didn’t care because I felt better.

Things went well until early last year when we started renovating our house and moved into a mobile in the garden. Stress piled up, but I coped well. Then I got pregnant with my second baby and decided to stop Lexapro after a previous miscarriage. Pregnancy was rough. The house was falling apart—mould, rats, outages, burst pipes, unreliable labourers—and my relationship was under strain. My partner worked full time while fixing the house, and I constantly complained of pain, stress, and depression. It was overwhelming.

Finally, we moved back into the house, and a few weeks later, our beautiful son was born! Things calmed down, and we were in a blissful bubble.

When our baby was four weeks old, I got a call that my dad (who lives in another country) had fallen ill. I flew out, and he spent a month in a coma. I visited him daily, which took a toll on my mental health. I wanted to avoid meds while breastfeeding, so I suffered through depression. Amazingly, my dad recovered and went home after three months.

Back home, our house was still half-finished, and our baby’s room wasn’t ready. We got to work and started to feel good again. But two weeks later, I got another call—my 18-year-old brother was in the hospital. I flew out the next day, but within days, he passed away from a ruptured bowel. It was devastating.

Since returning home, I cry every day. The grief is unbearable. Four weeks ago, my leg started hurting, triggering my health anxiety. I’ve convinced myself I have a blood clot, even though the doctor thinks it’s sciatica and scheduled a spine scan for January. The intrusive thoughts won’t stop.

Recently, I had a panic attack while alone with my son. I felt calm, then suddenly dizzy, with chest buzzing, difficulty breathing, and diarrhea. It lasted an hour. I begged my partner to take me to the hospital, then changed my mind. I knew it was probably anxiety but kept going back and forth. Now, my whole body feels tense. My neck, arm, leg, veins, and brain all hurt. I feel like I’m going insane.

I’m breastfeeding and don’t want to stop, but I want to live a happy life with my kids. Lexapro helped before, but the first month was hell. My baby is only six months old.

I’d love to hear advice or shared experiences. My life feels chaotic, but I know I’m incredibly blessed and just want to be happy and healthy.

Help understanding by Diagnosis
Hi everyone, I would normally not turn to reddit for something like this, as I am a big believer in not self-diagnosing or allowing yourself to be diagnosed by anyone other than a medical professional but I really am feeling hopeless and confused at this point. I'm going to explain my situation, and then if you feel comfortable with it, I would really appreciate any insight or suggestions.

SO. I have been in therapy for around 6 years. It started because at around 16/17, I began experiencing intense mood swings, anger, emptiness and self hatred. I have always had a difficult relationship with myself, but it was around this time that it seemed to blow up. I was also struggling with an ED. I initially went to my pediatrician and they just immediately put me on sertraline and happily diagnosed me with anxiety. But this did nothing to help. I stayed on it though for about 2 years before I finally stopped taking it and spent a year and a half unmedicated. I stayed in talk therapy this whole time btw- but I just felt like it went nowhere. I lie a lot, not maliciously, but because I get bored and feel the need to tell people whatever I think will make me look interesting. I do this with therapists often so it can be difficult for talk therapy to be beneficial. 

I was in my sophomore year of college when I began experiencing extreme mood swings, anxiety, paranoia, and control issues. This is also important because I began to develop routines that I literally could not break without feeling insane. Not like "wash my hands five times" routines, but like thought routines, speaking to my boyfriend at the exact same time every night routines-- I needed to control everything around me to feel grounded and safe. 

I started feeling like I was being "followed" by numbers, which I know sounds ridiculous but that is legitimately what I felt. I saw the numbers 2 and 4 everywhere. I had a break down with my boyfriend in a hotel room because I was so worried something really bad was going to happen involving the numbers. He went to crack the window to let me get some fresh air but when he opened the blinds, I about died as a giant neon 4 was lit up directly across the street. Horrible coincidences ultimately reached a head with the biggest most egregious coincidence of them all: a close friend died in a crash on Rt 422, on 4/22/2022. I'm dead serious. 

I got in touch with a psychiatrist after this and explained everything. She diagnosed me with Bipolar disorder unspecified/cyclothymia. I started meds and felt like things were getting better. I was on them for about 5 months but then had an unfortunate unrelated medical episode and had to stop taking them. I was then launched into about 4 months of intense depression and psychotic behavior. I went back on the meds and have been more regulated but still struggling. I was just recently diagnosed with pure O ocd. 

I feel there is more to this. I do not have a sense of self. I literally cannot tell you anything about me that makes me me. I will change whatever I need to in order to get people to like me. I engage in attention seeking behavior. I cannot control my thoughts. I have SH in the recent past. I continue to indulge in a quiet ED. I lie constantly. I feel always on the edge of a breakdown.

Should also mention I am a high achieving individual. I am a well decorated scholar and writer, having been publishing and having won multiple awards. I pride myself in my intelligence.

i have no idea what to do and i don't want to keep trying different drugs. what would you do in my shoes?

Anyone Else Feel Completely Numb on SSRIs? Need Advice on Emotional Blunting After Depression
**TL;DR:** After switching SSRIs from Sertraline to Lexapro, and now to Prozac, I’m experiencing severe emotional blunting—feeling numb, disconnected, and struggling to feel joy. Seeking support and advice from anyone who’s been through similar feelings and has found hope or improvement.

**Hi all!** As the title suggests, does anyone here have experience with emotional blunting after a deep depression or from taking SSRIs? I keep questioning myself, wondering if I’ve always been like this, but I genuinely remember being much happier and more joyful in the past.

For context, I was on Sertraline, alternating between 50 and 100mg. About seven weeks ago, my doctor switched me to Lexapro at 20mg, which has been quite a rough journey. It’s ranged from feeling absolutely numb to experiencing intense anxiety and daily crying, only to return to feeling nothing at all.

Just two days ago, my doctor prescribed me Prozac at 20mg, so I stopped the Lexapro and made the switch. I’m feeling a little better now, although it still comes and goes in waves. However, I still feel like this emotional blunting is really intense right now.

Nothing seems to bring me joy. For example, I had dinner with an old friend today, and I found myself wanting to leave almost immediately. I wasn’t anxious—I just didn’t want to be there. He’s super funny and easy to talk to, but I just couldn’t engage. I’m experiencing this with my parents and partner as well; it feels like I’m constantly pretending to be happy, but inside, I just feel empty.

I’d really appreciate any words of encouragement or hearing from someone who’s been through something similar. It would be comforting to know if there’s light at the end of this tunnel.

Thanks for reading! :)

I think I have quiet BPD and I wanted to share my thoughts
To clarify this is not self diagnosing. I am writing this only as a way of venting and in hopes of people being able to relate or give advice. I am 18 and have been researching the quiet subtype of BPD, on and off for over a year. I think I fit the criteria for a diagnosis but obviously I was 17 when I started looking into this and even now at 18 I am quite young for a diagnosis. As well as this I am still on the NHS neurodevelopmental pathway for ASD and ADHD and have been waiting to see someone for over two years on this. 

I want to start this by telling you some of the things I was told after a brief psychiatric assessment that was given in February - may 2023. She wrote a discharge letter and briefly explained some of the issues I am dealing with as I told her in person and had written her an email explaining more. I am doing this because honestly, it's easier than explaining every facet myself and afterwards I'll fill in any of the gaps. 
 
I cnped the letter and then removed bits and pieces not relevant: 
“Josh is aged 17 and he is moving on to college to complete BTEC qualifications with a view perhaps to studying Architecture at university. Josh has struggled for some years in fully engaging with education. It is likely that his plans and aspirations may change over the coming years. He finds it difficult to focus on academic studies because of his long-standing psychological difficulties. Josh has been referred by his previous school, where he completed his GCSEs at the end of Year 11 in May/June 2022, to the NHS Neurodevelopmental Pathway. Josh and his mother perceive that Josh presents with symptoms of both a social communication disorder (ASD – ICD10 F84.0) and ADHD (ICD10 F90). 
 
Secondary to Josh’s underlying neurodevelopmental difficulties, Josh also presents with marked symptoms of anxiety and low mood. Josh presents with initial insomnia, struggling to get to sleep and therefore finding it difficult to get up the next day to participate in education and any relevant activities. Josh experiences symptoms of depersonalisation/derealisation. Josh experiences visual hallucinations, e.g. seeing what he describes as “shadow men” out of the corner of his eye which I think are related to symptoms of anxiety as Josh denies any experimentation or use of substances or alcohol. 
 
Josh presents with Gender Identity Disorder. He uses the Progestogen-only pill and wears binders. He is keen to be referred to a Gender Disorder Clinic that can prescribe hormone treatment as a first step before gender reassignment surgery.
 
In addition to Josh’s symptoms of anxiety and low mood, he also has symptoms of OCD (ICD10 F42). He has concerns about germs, and can worry that what he has been given to eat, even food cooked by his mother, may make him ill. Josh only eats a limited diet, focused primarily on pasta and cheese at his mother’s house and potato-based foods when he visits his father. 
 
Josh finds it difficult to make and maintain friends. He can be quite black and white in his approach, perfectionistic and rigid. Josh does not easily cope well with transitions or unexpected alterations to his routine. He struggles with eye contact and empathy and experiences a range of sensory sensitivities. Josh is also aware that he struggles to attend and concentrate, finds it hard to focus, can be disorganised and struggles to stay on task.
 
FAMILY HISTORY 
*mum* and *dad* during their relationship had two children:
 
• Josh, the subject of this letter, aged 17 and repeating Year 12 at Sixth Form College in September 2023. Josh has identified as being of male gender for some time and is hoping when he turns 18 for greater support from the Gender Identity Disorder Clinic. 
 
• *brother*, aged 15 and just completing Year 10 at Christleton High School. He has also been referred to the NHS Neurodevelopmental Pathway for ADHD/ASD assessments. 
 
FAMILY HISTORY OF PSYCHIATRIC DISORDER
 
*dad* presents with some symptoms of anxiety and depression and may present with symptoms of complex PTSD according to mother’s account as a result of his adverse early life experiences. 
 
*mum* suffered symptoms of PTSD and depression following a termination when she was aged 18. At 40 she experienced an acute psychotic episode and benefitted from intensive CBT, Sertraline SSRI antidepressant medication and support from her parents. 
 
Josh is already prescribed Promethazine 50mg at night by his GP to help him sleep.
 
PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT
  
Josh experiences marked emotional lability, at times being quiet, withdrawn and depressed, spending most of his time in his bedroom and at other times being restless, fidgety and unable to calm down and concentrate on studies or hobbies. Josh is aware from his own account that he struggles to make and maintain friends. The only person with whom he has a close relationship where he can be open about his experience of intrusive thoughts, visual hallucinations and thoughts of suicidal intent, is his boyfriend to whom he speaks on a daily basis. 
 
 
Josh’s mother wrote to me after my last session, describing Josh as being sad and depressed long-term Indeed, she said, “Always looked like he had the world on his shoulders, hated himself, felt he did not quite fit in. He was not like others. Withdraws in situations he finds difficult, even at family events either will not go or soon takes himself off into another room to be alone as it becomes too much. He is visibly anxious in social situations, does not like to be touched. He finds it hard to understand what others are thinking and feeling and hard to read other people’s emotions”. She also commented that Josh often found it so difficult to talk about his feelings and emotions that he would text her to express concerns, e.g. in relation to thoughts of suicidal intent rather than talking to her.
 
FORMULATION
 
It is, unfortunately, not possible to organise these assessments privately. A formal diagnosis of neurodevelopmental difficulties has not been reached following this initial assessment but it is evident that Josh has complex difficulties.
 
In the meantime, Josh would benefit from re-referral to Tier 3 CAMHS and the introduction of SSRI antidepressant medication such as Sertraline to help manage his anxiety. “

Should I take Sertraline after traumatic shrooms experience?
Hello, just a bit about me. I struggled with anxiety and depression in my teenage years. Started to have panic attacks in certain public speaking/performance situations when I was 16. Had bouts of therapy over the years but have always been quite high-functioning and got a good support network of family and friends.  
When I was 21, I took Sertraline 25mg for about a year. To be honest, I didn’t notice too much of a difference, and it had a negative impact on my sex drive (which continued even after I stopped taking it).  
Cut to this this year and I’ve been through a lot of change, much of it positive: I ended a five-year relationship that wasn’t stimulating me anymore, I moved back in with my parents, I started dating an amazing new woman, I quit my boring job to start a course in music production. Overall, I was excited, although quite burnt-out and stressed from all the change that had happened in a short space of time. I felt I was embracing a more loose, extroverted and spontaneous version of myself.   
So about four months ago, I decided to take a small dose of psylocibin chocolate with my friend. I’d read a lot about psylocibin, and thought it might give me an interesting perspective on life and my anxieties. And anyway, I was taking a very small dose so I wasn’t overly concerned with it having a major effect on me.   
I had a horrendously bad time. I immediately starting feeling very panicky, and I felt like all the negative beliefs I’d ever had about myself and the world were incredibly vivid, like the universe was confirming they were all true and I was a terrible person. I became incredibly paranoid, had terrible intrusive thoughts that I’d do something bad to my friend.   
The last four months since have been unlike anything I’ve ever experienced. They make my previous struggles with anxiety and depression seem like an absolute cakewalk. I have severe PTSD from the shrooms experience, every waking moment I’m thinking about it and flashing back to how I felt then. At first I was completely convinced I’d lost my mind, and that the shrooms had awakened some kind of schizophrenia/psychosis. I was convinced that because I’d lost my mind, I might do something terrible to my loved ones.  
I feel my sense of self has been completely shattered, I have this horrible pulsating negative feeling in my body all day. I feel almost completely unable to relate to the person I was before, like I’ve died in a way, and I’m now in hell. I feel disconnected from family and friends, things that used to give me joy (music/books/film/exercise) no longer do anything to me, or sometimes actively frighten me. I am hypersensitive, almost everything seems to scares me. I’ve completely lost all sense of safety - I can never relax my mind or body, no matter how much I try. I don’t trust my mind at all. I have trouble sleeping and insomnia increases my feelings of derealisation/detachment.  
I have had occasional days/weeks in the past four months where this feeling has receded and I’ve felt more myself/able to connect with people and hobbies again. But then the sinister feeling returns, and I’m plunged into full-on shrooms flashback for weeks at a time.  
I’ve had a particularly bad episode this week where I’ve felt very suicidal and hopeless.  
I’ve been having CBT to talk through the experience, but the thoughts and feelings are so extreme that it hasn’t really helped. I then got in touch with an EDMR therapist. I was so anxious to begin the first session in case it made me feel worse (this can happen). I expressed this to her and she thinks I’m actually too hyper anxious to start it.  
Her opinion is that I should take Sertraline to take the edge off things before starting EDMR in a few weeks.   


But I’m so panicked about taking Sertraline. I know that SSRIs can increase feelings of detachment/insomnia/suicidality at the beginning, and I just can’t bear the thought of feeling any worse than I do now.  
The way my brain works, the moment I swallow the pill I’ll be having a full-blown panic attack about its side effects, tracking every single thought, every feeling, every sensation, looking for evidence that I’m losing my mind more and doomed to kill myself.  
Unlike when I took Sertraline the first time, I have this new fear of drugs and changing my brain chemistry. I’ve already had it with sleeping pills. I know it sounds crazy but I think ‘What if I take this sleeping pill and my panic is so strong that it doesn’t work and then I get caught in a horrible liminal disassociated space? And what if I do something terrible in that space?’ And it basically came true when I took a sleeping pill (apart from the ‘doing something terrible’ bit).  
I know a lot of people with PTSD have had their symptoms eased with Sertraline, but my trauma comes from taking a psychoactive drug and the effect it had on my mind - so it’s a bit more of a complicated beast with me. I know that if I ride out the first couple of weeks it should have a positive effect, but I’m so terrified to have side effects.  
I felt pretty trapped and hopeless in my situation. Do you think I should take the Sertraline?

Hey,

Unsure if I should start medication again
Hi,

First of all I should clarify that I am a sufferer of OCD, and have been for eight years now. During these eight years, I was prescribed with medication (Sertraline/Zoloft) to deal with the symptoms of my OCD and help me recover from a period of depression.

This brings me to the predicament I am currently in. I have recently come off my medication in the hopes that I could go through life without taking a pill. For about 6-8 weeks I had experienced no withdrawals and I was doing relatively fine, with only a few minor complications. However, this week I've had a relapse of my OCD, and it has been the worst it has ever been than it has been in years. In short, I have had constant racing thoughts, worsened cognition (memory, concentration etc) and an overall depressed mood. All of which have affected my work and personal life.

Now here's the tricky or annoying part for myself and my family, which has existed even BEFORE I stopped my medication, and is what made me want to stop in the first place. I have this "belief" that it is shameful to take medication for my condition, and that I should deal with it using only therapy and a healthy lifestyle (exercise, healthy eating etc). There is also conspiratorial aspects as well. I have these "beliefs" (or "worries") that suggest that the medication is harming me and my brain. That it has affected my cognitive ability over the years when I was growing up, and that it has also made me emotionally numb (a big factor in my "worries"). It is annoying to have these "worries", because in some ways I believe them, and in some ways I don't. It is almost as if my OCD has manifested into these thoughts and is essentially stopping me from getting any help.

This predicament has seriously affected me and my family. For myself, I'm worried that this continious playing with the medication (reducing dosage/coming off over the course of over a year) and my ailing mental condition has severly affected me emotionally and cognitively. My biggest concern is that this situation has affected my intelligence and memory permanently and as a result I have been "mentally stunted".

Please any advice would be much appreciated. I honestly don't know what to do. I am uncertain of what to do and have no clear direction to follow.

Will I find myself again? [mom/wife]
Hello, first post here —

31, F, mom of 2 amazing little boys ages 5 and 1.5, married to the most amazing man of 8 years.

There’s a lot to unpack here!  Why am I having the hardest time finding ME again?  I’m a great mother, there is no doubt.  That will always come first.  But everything else has been put on the back burner.  I know “me” is not the same “me” that I was 5 years ago, but I have struggled a lot (especially after baby #2) with the following:

1. Sex life - I am NOT interested. I cannot get myself to barely find joy in it at all.  And then I feel horrible for my husband.  My husband tries to understand and he has never made me feel bad, but I know this affects him on a much deeper level. 

2. Exercising - I love to exercise. I was a 3 sport athlete in high school and continued on through college.  But now my motivation is incredibly low. 

3. Low self esteem/depression/closet eating - I recently started seeing a psychiatrist for all of this.  I was diagnosed with ADHD and have been switching around my depression medications trying to figure out something that may help with my low libido.  I feel so hopeful that there will be change in all the above, but I just can’t get there! It got better for awhile, but then I fell off the wagon again recently which just adds more of my issue (I will post all my medications below).

4. Poor spending habits - I think online shopping/eating out is something I do (ADHD?) to “fill a void” when I’m in a lull. 

5. Finding time for just me or just me and my husband - I feel like I make excuses for any opportunity given to have time to myself or time to ourselves for a date.  I’m not sure if this is for feeling guilty?  Guilty for being able to do just 1 more load of laundry, to cut the grass, to clean out my car, etc.  There’s always “something” else I could be doing that seems to be worth my time. 

Like I said before, my babies are taken care of.  I have a wonderful support system. I am a nurse and now have flexible hours and recently (5 months ago) quit an extremely hostile job that I’d been at for nearly 10 years.  I just want to help find me again. I want to be able to love my husband like he deserves to be loved. It’s like a keep that part of me partially locked up and I won’t let it out… if that makes sense.  

These are my current medications I’m on: enskyce (birth control pills), Wellbutrin 300 mg (depression), Vyvanse 40 mg (ADHD), Losartan/HCTZ (blood pressure - weaning off), Topamax 50 mg (binge eating), and recently started Desvenlafaxine/Pristiq 25 mg (depression).  I had been on Sertraline for a few months but she contributed that to my low libido.  I have high hopes for Pristiq as I was reading it has helped many women who are postpartum.  

I appreciate you reading this long note and I appreciate any kind words or advice you may have ❤️

15yo me:
When I was 15 started a terrible obsesiveness treated with sertraline, AP and Benzo that sent me Into an hypomanic state but cured me. Then put in sodium valproate (for mood stabilization) and risperidone. Was anxious and with Focusing problems unattended, as far as I understand pdoc didnt wanted to risk with more medication for a posible manic episode but always talked to her about it and just increased/decreased valproate/risperidone to treat that.

2015 (18yo me)

Was anxious, socially anxious/awkard with focusing problems.
Consumed weed at 18 while on medication and panic disorder erupted. Treated with benzos again, so far I was ok; then continued anxious state happened, pdoc1 added fluvoxamine to the combo, felt like didnt work and changed pdoc; then with this doc started slowly tappering off mood stabilizer and risperidone and introducing Zoloft which worked in about a couple Of months and was really good. After this, entered into a long sustained good feeling state until 2018.

2018 (21yo): 
Hypomania and alcohol/no sleeping gave me a psychosis/paranoia that lasted a day at its peak and left me a bad feeling for a month or so. Somehow my brain changed and I became overly religious (kinda schizo but not sure)

2019 (22yo):

Had focusing issues but while in this state managed myself to focus and work hard in the company I was working back then, which resulted in a free trip to China and upraisal. Started feeling some numbness in my emotions/thought, manageable though, but all along uncomfortable.

2020 (23yo):
I stopped the meds first time, didnt taper them off properly . Just as I stopped them, racing thoughts come by, body temperature changing by minute and it was noticeable in my face. So reinstated and everything worked not too well, but worked, had many focus issues and lost emotions then, but at least was able to be functional and enjoy life somewhat. 

Then 2022 happened, meet this girl, had a lot of sex and weed, with the numbness of emotion/thought and also sudden rushes of weakness wanted to stop Zoloft and we made a plan to do it very slowly in a year…then shit happens… as I tappered it a little bit (12.5mg or so) while smoking, my brain managed to snap and became psychotic/paranoid, 

somehow in that state as I was kinda concious stopped the weed bc was making me slow… and fully stopped Zoloft too (because oc the Holy Spirit told me to 🧙🏻‍♂️) and well…

My parents talked to the pdoc and they managed to gave me risperidone without noticing, which stopped my actions and reduced the delusion (it is worth to mention that in psychosis I also felt terrible body pain, tremors and pins a needles that I attributed to witchcraft the bad guys where doing to me oc), but when I came to “reality”also felt terrible left me without a soul, it just crushed everything I though I had and left me in a state of pure agony second by second.

No sleep , the worst numbness that will made me wake up in the middle of the night to pace until morning, just wanting to die each second of existence, no joy, no emotion, no body feelings, weird body feelings, racing thoughts, not able to lay in bed, intensely pacing through the day(it’s some kind of weird akathisia but more a feeling of desestimulation and dizziness that is just unbearable to lay in bed/sleep), derealization, intense anhedonia, weird thought dizziness (like my head spinning with thoughts), dizziness itself, weak thoughts, changing my mind through the day, weird time sensation, perception issues of space, socially desensitized.

So I requested the pdoc to give me an ssri (bc didn’t know what else to do) and he gave me paxil because of Zoloft shortage, so far Paxil reduced 10% of the continued agony, and nothing else. Took Zoloft liquid (as it’s the only one available) 75 mg for a month reduced the agony 25% (not anxiety, even though it appears as a slow painful anguish feeling, just restlessness, finding no comfort in no place), just raised to 100mg and it feels like I’m going forward for a reduced agony of 40%.

Right now I’m taking this:

Started Zoloft exactly one month and a half ago with 75mg with reduced agony of 25%. I stopped Zoloft for a period of 5 months or so. Raised to 100mg 6 days ago and can lay in bed for more time and somehow sleep through night.

Also I’m taking 0.5 Ativan at night 

The pdoc sent me Sodium Valproate but I’m not sure to take it because of my condition being critical don’t wanna mess it up.

So what’s next what can you tell me about this mess? What could work? What doesn’t?

So far Zoloft reinstating it’s working, how much you think convenient based on your experience to raise the dose and when…

Can substances induce week-long "psychosis"? My experience and your opinion

Preface: I've had problems of light depression for years, on and off, very rarely I've had anxiety, I've never had a panic attack. TW: drugs, anxiety

My experience of almost three years ago: I was going through a rough time sentimentally and was overall in a bad place. On NYE I mixed a slightly higher than "usual" amount of substances that definitely shouldn't be mixed - alcohol, cocaine and MDMA all together, not in huge quantities but I'm very small, Idk. My body immediately had a strong reaction - threw up, couldn't sleep, then for a couple of days I was fine. Then the most HORRIFIC experience of my life started and lasted for around 40-50 days. I stopped sleeping. I experienced HUGE anxiety every second that I was awake, paranoia, super intrusive thoughts, my stomach was completely shut and I lost 4 kg in 2 weeks. I was still "myself" and could kinda function socially but it required every ounce of my strength and will. I was kind of frozen in panic, from what I've read about panic attacks they're different: this felt acute just ALL the time, imagine someone making a prank on you and you JUMP in scare. This feeling, this state of sudden and brief panic, but ongoing for longer than a month. I felt like I had no walls to protect my subconscious, I had horrific nightmares which literally felt REAL, I was deeply depressed and thinking I could never be happy again. I showered twice in a month because I couldn't be alone in a room, I was super scared of being alone in a room. I moved to a friend's house and she took care of me. She cooked and did everything that I needed, I was restless, I couldn't watch a movie or read a book or watch the news or anything because they gave me strong anxiety and I thought I would just go crazy. I experienced STRONG depersonalization and that was the most horrible thing I've ever felt.

I started taking benzodiazepines and a light dose (50 mg) of antidepressants (sertraline) and they worked very well, in around a month the anxiety stopped and I could sleep and live again.

I'm SURE that all this was due to the drug use, BUT my therapist/psychiatrist says that the chemical residue of drugs disappears from the brain in a couple of days, they're just not there anymore. So it must have been "me" or "my brain" making all this mess, not the drugs. I can't reconcile this idea with the brutality of this experience (my brain did this without drugs?) and Im scared it might happen again even w/o substances.

is it your experience too that substances can unclench even week-long "psychoses"? I don't know what to make of this. Does anyone have an explanation? I guess I just want to be safe that I wont have to go through the same thing again ever ...

Why do I get so extremely depressed in the afternoon and evening.
So I have had a long battle with mental illness starting about 7-8 years ago in my early teens. I am currently in the best place I've ever been which is good. I have gone from unproductive, smoking pot all day and having 4-6 beers in the evening to calm down my depressive states to for the most part, sober with extended lengths of sobriety and cutting down usage when I do have a lapse, but even before the substance use as a coping strategy I get this weird thing where no matter how I feel waking up in the morning, no matter how productive I am, or unproductive, I feel like absolute dog shit in the evening and night up until I fall asleep. This has been ongoing since my mental illness started when I was 12/13.

But the funny thing is when I wake up in the morning I am rational, In a good mood most of time if no external factors are feeding into the depression, ready to get started for the day and feeling this sense of control over my emotions and thoughts, and better able to rationalize and move onto to a distraction or a more calming thought.

I have also got OCD which is also a factor, but that seems to be bordering pretty close to full remission with no compulsions, and maybe 0-3 intrusive thoughts a day.  

It is just so frustrating because once it gets to 2-3pm I start to see a decrease in mood, by 4-5pm I am In a state where the world feels so dull and lack of any meaning. I then start worrying about stuff that has happened or I feel like my drive to live just decreases rapidly, I don't become suicidal per say but It becomes a lot easier to rationalize the thought that things feel dull and meaningless and that things aren't ever going to improve, which is funny because before this mind state that kicks in at this time (It is currently 7pm) I am able to rationalize that everything is getting better and improving. 

It is so frustrating because of my bpd and adhd I become a lot more impulsive at this time and I feel the urge to have a beer even though it will just put me in a worse state.

please give some advice if you can about this or share your experiences and coping strategies or just let me know if you experience a similar phenomenon.  

I am also on Medication for depression and other forms of mental health

\- Zoloft (sertraline) 150mg in the morning

\- clonidine 100 mcg 3 times a day for ADHD, non-stimulant ( doesn't cause a crash)

\-Seroquel 50-100mg depending on my ability to get to sleep that night (50mg for a therapeutic dose working in conjunction with Zoloft for OCD and BPD and Depression, and an extra 50mg (100mg total) for sleep if needed ( I can't take over 100mg of Seroquel because of intense derealization and Intense anxiety from feeling zombified) so upping a dose isn't an option.
