Can depression stunt romantic attraction?
Hi all, I hope this is okay to ask here. First of all I do have a history of depression and anxiety and have been on sertraline a few times in my life since I was 16, most recently in 2020-21, so I've been off meds for a while.

I just want to preface this post by saying I don't think my sex drive has changed. I know depression can affect your libido, I always had a lower sex drive than my peers but I am in fact not asexual. I'm just not one of those people that must have sex at any cost if it's been "too long" or whatever, but I can and do feel arousal, sexual desire, etc, just don't necessarily need to act on it and for me that's always been normal, with or without medication. So that's not my concern!

What I *am* worried about is *romantic* attraction. I have been struggling to feel it for the past couple of years, especially this year. I see people that are objectively beautiful, they're attractive, just... not to me. I don't find them *un*attractive either, I can tell they look good and all... I just don't feel any type of way about them. At all. I did briefly have a crush on someone this summer and nothing came of it (we were at a festival, she was there with her boyfriend, I'm a lesbian, it clearly wasn't meant to be lol) but I literally had to just go have a little cry from sheer relief because I was starting to get scared that I'm dead inside. But it hasn't happened again since and it's... scary.

Is this a depression thing? 

I also genuinely can't tell how depressed I am or am not at this point because I've been living with this for almost half my life now so even when I'm depressed I've learned plenty of coping skills and just kinda carry on as best I can. I've definitely had some heavy depressive episodes this year but it's getting hard to tell what's the actual depression and what's just a normal response to things - I've dealt with unemployment and the industry I'm in becoming increasingly insecure (it's something I really love doing as well so it's been a bit of an identity crisis lol), I've had some family stuff to deal with too, then there's obviously the enormity of just Current Events... I genuinely can't tell if I'm depressed or having a very normal response to what's going on. And could either of those things be affecting my ability to feel attraction? 

Any thoughts appreciated! Thanks!

So I met this girl. Spent the whole of lockdown with her. She has borderline personality disorder, but she got me, and I got her. I have never been so happy. 
Then she got gallstones, she was in so much pain I was scared to touch her, I won’t into details, but It meant certain parts of our relationship were on hold, I get that. After about a year, she had emergency surgery, and they removed her gall bladder, which helped, but the scarring was still causing immense pain. I was also going through depression, and was prescribed Sertraline, which I am still on the max dose of. I am sure there are people on here that know the side effects that this causes in men. To put it mildly, sex was totally off the cards. 
Fast forward a few months, and we had a blazing row (on New Years Day) and I was told that “sex was shit”, and given no opportunity to reply, and short of a couple of 2 minute conversations, she will not speak to me, “apparently I will thank her for this one day”.
I seriously thought about taking my life last Christmas, I had COVID the week before and so my Christmas plans were on hold, thankfully, I was better by Christmas and did not spend it alone. 
I am a 57 year old man who has only ever found love once, and until I get over her, I doubt I ever will. I was losing weight before I met her (she never had an issue with my weight) and was very confident. I’m now 25 stone, zero self confidence and on the precipice between loving and hating her. I will never get over her until I meet someone else I will never meet someone else until I get over her.
Was I just someone that was there to look after her when no better options were available, or did she love me, I’ll never know till she speaks to me, and that looks like it won’t happen. I have slept alone for over a year, some nights crying myself to sleep, I really see not point in continuing. I now know that there is fine line between love and hate, and have reached a crossroads in life where there is no path available that appeals.

Sertraline/Zoloft - Stuck
Hi everyone,

I’ve been seeing a therapist for the past three years, and while it’s been incredibly helpful, I feel like I’ve hit a wall. I’m not making the progress I hoped for, especially when it comes to reducing my anxiety.

I’ve dealt with anxiety my whole life—primarily social anxiety, but also performance anxiety. For example, I recently had a job interview. For two weeks leading up to it, I barely left the house except for work. The day before, I broke down crying because I felt so unprepared. On the day of the interview, I cried again and felt like I wanted to stop existing because it was too overwhelming to handle.

Even though I went through with the interview, my anxiety caused me to self-sabotage. The moment the call ended, I realized all the mistakes I’d made. I know I could have done better without this overwhelming anxiety.

My therapist has recommended trying sertraline (Zoloft), but I’m torn. I’ve heard mixed things—some people say it helps a lot, especially in the beginning, but others warn that at some point, you end up paying for it one way or another, whether through side effects or other challenges.

I’m at a point where I’m not sure what to do. Have any of you taken sertraline for anxiety? What was your experience like? Did it help, and how did you manage any downsides?

Thanks in advance for your insights—I really appreciate any advice or personal stories you can share!

Severe treatment resistant depression, and I'm struggling not to lose hope.
Hey friends. I don't know why I'm posting this, if just to cry somewhere and feel heard or what. I don't know. Everything feels pointless right now.

I've got severe, chronic treatment-resistant depression. The only times I've ever had any alleviation of symptoms was when I found a medication that worked, it would work a few years maybe, then it stops working. It's been fifteen years. I'm only 25, and I already feel as if all hope is lost, tbh.

I've tried about ten antidepressants, from a range of families - they all either didn't work at all or worked for a while, then stopped working. I've tried mood stabilisers, quetiapine, had electroconvulsive therapy which didn't work. TMS and VNS aren't offered here, apparently. I was inpatient for about six weeks because of my depression and they put me back on two meds that worked for me before but stopped working, though this time in combination (40mg mirtazapine and 200mg sertraline). I'm currently in ketamine therapy and I feel *something* from it, but it's not what I'd get from functioning antidepressants.

The next steps are moclobemide, lamotrigine, and lithium. I'm in therapy and will also get help for comorbid OCD when I'm stable in my depression but honestly? I feel like it's a lost cause. I know, logically, these meds might work and I haven't tried MAOIs (honestly though, I'd rather just end things than deal with those diet changes - I know it sounds super overdramatic but the bar is just so low for me and I love food, lol) - but I feel so hopeless. Am I going to spend the rest of my life trying meds that work temporarily and then stop? What if nothing works, am I just doomed to live this way?

People hear my story and remind me how lucky I am - and I *am* so lucky. Which makes me feel horribly guilty for being the way that I am, on top of survivor's guilt and everything from past experiences. I'm seeing a therapist and I'm slowly understanding myself better but without medication I cannot survive. It's been 15 years and I know that for a fact - I need medication to be able to live.

I've completely lost who I am. Everything that I was passionate about, I feel nothing for. I'm like a different person, although over 15 years I've learned how to fake it so people don't see it - but I know.

I'm just so, so exhausted. I feel so hopeless, I feel like it's all pointless. I'm so tired. I'm sorry to whine.

Lost
Throughout my childhood I never thought I would be depressed, depression is not something I really talk about with my family or friends has its not really something that can be understood by everyday beings and is usually interpreted wrongly, an attention seeker, you're just sad, you're just having a bad day.

in 2017 I had severe anxiety and my mother had to request a home visit from the doctor over concerns I wanted to kill myself, when did my depression start? like many people it usually starts with bad events, i'm not looking for attention I just kinda want to voice my story.

  
When I finished secondary school (UK's equivalent to Highschool) the transition to college was tough, being 16 I lacked many social skills and was placed into a class of fully grown adults (30+) for my electrical engineering course, now being so young I was in no doubt the "od" one out, my first day I ended up vomiting all on the class floor, nerves? fear? perhaps, but it most certainly didn't help, being bullied in high school didnt help my social confidence, I was made fun of being skinny and having a slightly larger head, doesn't help having a small frame, another thing for "those" people to pick on at the time.

Going back to college I was failing my exams, the transition was a massive jump for me personally, no friends, everything failing so I dropped out and fell into the comfort of my bedroom where no one can judge me and I don't have to face the results of my failure, my bedroom being my small bubble.

  
over the next few years I fell in love with world of warcraft, it was the game for me to pass time and forget about life, everyday tasks felt like such a mission, again everyday people call it laziness but mentally the simplest tasks felt impossible, personal hygiene, cleaning my room, collection of dishes etc.

  
Eventually I got to a point of where I wanted to change, I forced myself outside to try and build social skills with people, I did this by going up to people and asking if they had the time, stupid yes but in todays age strangers are you know, strangers, I kept working on myself with the assistance of sertraline, going to the gym at 3:00 am, empty but a few people and slowly climbed my way up.

  
I was out, few years later I was employed, anxiety gone, no longer on sertraline and met a loving girlfriend & that ive been with for 3 years & finally learnt to drive and purchased my own car, however I now feel im sinking back into my old life, over the last month or two I genuinley feel myself sinking into quicksand, I write tasks that I need to complete but it feels impossible, im mentally drained and exhaused and im asking myself whether or not I need to go back onto sertraline, 

  
With depression does it come in waves? is it down to life events that makes it come back? is it always dormant in us?

My depression and anxiety story and current experience with moclobemide (long post)
Moclobemide quite detailed experience after 3 weeks of being on it. Also I tell u my story before so you have a bigger picture of me and my issues. It will be a long pots so if u not ready just skip it.

Hello . I’m 23 years old male. All my hormone levels are in range and I’m physically healthy.
I struggled with anxiety and low grade atypical depression throughout my life and always had social problems , always felt not confident, different from others . My little brother got diagnosed with adhd and he is 9 years old so I am waiting for a diagnosis. and docs were thinking he has mild autism (aspengers) but weren’t diagnosed.

Since my young years I used to always chase everything that gives me dopamine. I was playing computer games for 14 hours in a day for a few years because it was giving me so much dopaminergic pleasure and It always made me distracted from my low moods and anxietys so possibly a coping mechanism. I also been overeating always since young age and I would eat until I feel sick sometimes so possibly compulsive eating (my brother does the same thing now , playing loads of games , overeating (he weight 60 kg at 9 years old which is not healthy ) and watching tv all the time so he reminds me of myself as a kid .

I had drug use issues with mostly cannabis and ecstasy (took too much in 1 month and possibly some some neuronal damage ) .
I abused weed heavily for 3-4 years since 17 because it was helping me with depression and not caring about things. 

In 2021 I quit everything except cigarettes and coffee and my anxiety was bad. Almost like paranoid anxiety and I developed anhedonia. I can’t get the same type of pleasure from anything I do like I used to before and I think part of it is growing up.

Since 2021 I tried sertraline(helped with anxiety but made me fearless and made anhedonia worse which made me do crazy things to chase any kind of adrenaline rush or use drugs ) , venlafaxine (fucked me up) , Wellbutrin (helped but made anxiety very bad and bad tinnitus and visual snow ) , citalopram (useless) , buspirone (helped with anxiety a lot but brain fog was bad , made me feel lobotomised) , pregabalin for anxiety(was effective for my anhedonia and I mean extremely effective , 150 without tolerance made me so euphoric and gave me childhood vibes but I rarely take is because it won’t help me long term for sure and I get rebounds after I take it few days in a row .

My diagnosis right now (confirmed ) depressive anxious disorder , emotionally unstable personality disorder . Also waiting for adhd diagnosis . There are the ones confirmed by the doctor.

Now unconfirmed but this is what I’m feeling.
Bad anhedonia , light ocd, bad health anxiety and sometimes even paranoia, atypical depression (mood is low 80 percent of the time but is reactive to positive things happening)



Since I’m also novelty seeker, for 3 years I extensively researched pharmacology and mental health problems and I came to conclusion that my main problem is dopamine. Modafinil 100 mg got rid of my anhedonia completely for 3 days so I would assume that I would need something that increases serotonin to help with anxiety and dopamine to treat my boredom in everything, lack of drive , anhedonia , low motivation and so on.

the only antidepressants on the market that can increase dopamine are maois and since I live in the UK it’s almost impossible to get it through nhs . 

Also I have to mention that since I have severe health anxiety and cardiophobia I’m very scared of irreversibles as the side effects can be really bad so I decided to trial moclobemide but as I thought they refused because they said it’s an old medication and can be dangerous.

I have researched moclobemide for 1 year and I came to conclusion that it’s relatively safe if you being mindful and looking after possible interactions. 

I have ordered Turkish moclobemide (deva brand ) 19th of January 2024 from online pharmacy and I only started taking it 20-22 days ago.


Here is my experience so far.

Week 1 - felt increase in energy and neutralisation of my depression that persisted until now. Didn’t feel serotonergic but very wired feeling and very noradrenergic. My strength increased a lot as my gym gains increased rapidly so I guess it really does increase testosterone. My libido increase as well and orgasm got stronger. Social anxiety decreased a lot and I feel calmer in crowded places. sometimes I would get little brain fog and dissociation but only the first weeek and now I don’t have it . The only side effect I had were dry mouth after taking the pill for a few hours and insomnia , I can fall asleep fine but I wake up early and only sleep 4-6 hours . It also decreased my heart rate a bit from 58 to 50-52 and made my sympathetic nervous system calmer as well.

Week 2 the effects were the same so was a bit more active but I felt like I need to increased the dose so I increased to 450.
When I was taking 300 in the morning it was making me feel very sleepy and dizzy so I guess it reduces bpm but I didn’t check it that time.

First few days on 450 were fine except quite poor sleep and nightmares but on the fourth day I decided for some stupid reason to have a coffee right before taking 300 mg in the morning and 1-2 hours later I felt manic with loads of energy , very bad physical anxiety and inability to sit still so I popped some bromonorgiazepam (gidazepam) and I calmed down. The anxiety was physical only and not mental . Feels like I have too much energy so it probably greatly increased the effects of caffeine . Firstly I blamed. Hello . I’m 23 years old male. All my hormone levels are in range and I’m physically healthy.
I struggled with anxiety and low grade atypical depression throughout my life and always had social problems , always felt not confident, different from others . My little brother got diagnosed with adhd and he is 9 years old so I am waiting for a diagnosis. and docs were thinking he has mild autism (aspengers) but weren’t diagnosed.

Since my young years I used to always chase everything that gives me dopamine. I was playing computer games for 14 hours in a day for a few years because it was giving me so much dopaminergic pleasure and It always made me distracted from my low moods and anxietys so possibly a coping mechanism. I also been overeating always since young age and I would eat until I feel sick sometimes so possibly compulsive eating (my brother does the same thing now , playing loads of games , overeating (he weight 60 kg at 9 years old which is not healthy ) and watching tv all the time so he reminds me of myself as a kid .

I had drug use issues with mostly cannabis and ecstasy (took too much in 1 month and possibly some some neuronal damage ) .
I abused weed heavily for 3-4 years since 17 because it was helping me with depression and not caring about things. 

In 2021 I quit everything except cigarettes and coffee and my anxiety was bad. Almost like paranoid anxiety and I developed anhedonia. I can’t get the same type of pleasure from anything I do like I used to before and I think part of it is growing up.

Since 2021 I tried sertraline(helped with anxiety but made me fearless and made anhedonia worse which made me do crazy things to chase any kind of adrenaline rush or use drugs ) , venlafaxine (fucked me up) , Wellbutrin (helped but made anxiety very bad and bad tinnitus and visual snow ) , citalopram (useless) , buspirone (helped with anxiety a lot but brain fog was bad , made me feel lobotomised) , pregabalin for anxiety(was effective for my anhedonia and I mean extremely effective , 150 without tolerance made me so euphoric and gave me childhood vibes but I rarely take is because it won’t help me long term for sure and I get rebounds after I take it few days in a row .

My diagnosis right now (confirmed ) depressive anxious disorder , emotionally unstable personality disorder . Also waiting for adhd diagnosis . There are the ones confirmed by the doctor.

Now unconfirmed but this is what I’m feeling.
Bad anhedonia , light ocd, bad health anxiety and sometimes even paranoia, atypical depression (mood is low 80 percent of the time but is reactive to positive things happening)

It can make physical anxiety worse but it helps tremendously with mental anxiety and I find the will power to brush off my anxieties and be more present and realistic about the situation.

Anxiety of taking pills
I, 22M, have been on Escitalopram for depression (no anxiety) with almost no side effects and prescribed Xanax for emergencies. After some time the escitalopram stopped working and I started taking paroxetine, which worsened my condition, and after a dose increase it completely messed me up and I had started tapering off of it. Even with the tapering process I became ill due to severe withdrawal symptoms which I suffered through for a week until I could get an appointment with my GP. The doctor claimed I have unexpectedly high susceptibility to this sort of medications (SSRIs) and dosage increase/tapering should be done more gradually than usual. So I started taking sertraline which helped my depression but made me nauseous (beyond the usual 2 weeks of normal side effects) and also, based on what other people told me, made me quite aggressive and irritable. So I went back to escitalopram, but a new psychiatrist that I decided to visit decided that I should go off escitalopram and start taking fluoexetine, he suggested I drop the 10 mg of escitalopram I was on (in the beginning I was at max dose of 20 mg) for two days and start the new drug, I explained what happened with the paroxetine and that I don't think I can go through this sort of extreme withdrawal again, so he suggested I taper off of it by taking 5 mg for 10 days, wait 2 days and then star the fluoexetine. Two days after I lowered the dose I became sick again, due to withdrawal (recognized it right away) and it was WAY worse than the first time, I was unable to function let alone go to work. I live alone and quite far from my parents, don't really have any close friends, and I was having non-stop crying fits and panic attacks, nausea, diarrhea even puked a couple of times due to stress. I tried to reach the psychiatrist but to no avail...I had to go back to my parents as I was afraid of harming myself, the psychiatrist answered my message a week later asking why I was even taking the escitalopram when he instructed me to take fluoexetine...I had a piece of paper with his instructions where what I previously wrote was clearly stated...I found a new and expensive psychiatrist and went to her for guidance and she suggested I take mirtazapine, but I couldn't do it. Every pill I take, even ones I took before (Xanax even) make me anxious to the point of panicking out of fear from having a bad reaction or even an allergic reaction (which I have only had for penicilin when I was 7, once), I never had anxiety before and even the Xanax was for when I feel extreme sadness and not for anxiety, so now I have anxiety too and I am afraid of taking the new pills and am kinda lost...Any suggestions on how to move forward from here will be appreciated. 
To be clear, when I realized the psychiatrist, who barely took family history from me and mocked me for the reason I was depressed during our meeting, didn't remember his own medication plan I didn't bother taking the fluoexetine and simply waited on 5 mg of escitalopram until my meeting with the new psychiatrist, which was today.

I have OCD and maybe anxiety/depression. I'm on sertraline and have been for over a year now at a pretty low dose. Not sure what to do. Just venting ig? Idk

Off of Sertraline for 3 weeks. Life update. Need help.
Took 100mg Sertraline for panic disorder for over a year and I finally tapered off it by taking 50 mg and then 25mg. Took 50 mg for about 5 months and then 25mg over a period of time (not sure how long but probably 1-2 months). So this is my 3 weeks-in update. First week felt almost same as I did while on meds, 2nd week started feeling a little weird, spaced out, disconnected, kind of like a dazed state of mind. 3rd week is the worst so far, lightheaded, dazed feeling is becoming really strong. The feeling of losing balance while walking is scary. Brain zaps right as I am about to fall asleep, none while awake. 
I took Propranolol along with it for migraines which does seem to help quite a bit so I'm continuing taking it. Also, I am aware of the interaction btw Sertraline and propranolol.
I feel fine otherwise, panic attacks are fairly under control. More from learning and getting used to it than anything else really. Although SSRIs did help initially to control these panic feelings. I am reaching out here on Reddit for help. What can I expect from being off of Sertraline in the coming days? Will it continue to get worse for me? I really don't want to get back on it as I am fairly in control of my panic attacks. Please advise.

Insomnia/depression/antidepressant/libido
Hi all! I've (27, male) been suffering from depression and anxiety most of my life (still being treated by psychologist). Fortunately, most of the time my mental issues are controllable. However, as soon as I enter a spiral of anxiety induced insomnia, my mood deteriorates and I often become depressed. Sertraline/Zoloft (50/100 mg) is a life safer for me because it significantly reduces my depressed mood and elevates most of my insomnia symptoms. At the same time, as a side effect, I lose my libido and sometimes feel like an emotional zombie while being on these meds. Therefore, I have decided to go off Zoloft (again), particularly in the light of having a new (loving) partner. Nowadays, my insomnia is back (after successfully and gradually withdrawing from Zoloft 3 months ago) and I believe I'm starting to get trapped again in the insomnia-anxiety-depression spiral. Therefore, I have a few questions for you:

* Do you have any non-standard tips for depression/anxiety induced insomnia? I believe good sleep is het corner stone for my mental health.

* Would you recommend any antidepressants that have lower sexual side effects that would have the same positive effect on my sleeping behavior?

Thanks!

Treatment-Resistant Depression: Dosage Adjustment
Hi there!

I am a 21-year old guy who has a history of Generalized Anxiety Disorder; got treated with 100 mg of Sertraline (Zoloft) for 1.5 years. I restarted using Sertraline (100-150 mg interchangeably) and Amitriptyline 10 mg for four months for Adjustment Disorder and Irritable Bowel Syndrome, but Amitriptyline made me put up weight, thus, I moved to Duloxetine (Cymbalta)-60 mg and 2.5 mg of Aripiprazole (Abilify) for treatment-resistant depression. Cymbalta works great (nearly 100% reduction in IBS-D symptoms, especially agonizing bowel pain) for IBS, but it doesn't feel like it works well enough as an antidepressant. Thus, I needed to take a-low-dose antipsychotic augmentation.

My question is for firstly mental health professionals and secondly for the Cymbalta users: I do feel like I am a fast-drug metabolizer (not supported by genetic profiling, but, conventional doses aren't as effective as for mean population for me generally). And I don't want to try another antidepressant as Cymbalta is great for IBS-related pain reduction. But as far as I searched PubMed, Doses above 60 mg/day doesn't confer any additional benefit.

What are your opinions about increasing the Cymbalta regimen from 60 mg/day to 90 mg/day?

When I started sertraline, I had horrible racing heart, nausea, and uncontrollable diarrhea.

The racing heart made me feel like i was on hard drugs and I would have to remove myself from whatever I was doing to go home and be in a safe feeling place while the racing heart passed.

The nausea wasn't so bad, but I found out very quickly drinking alcohol was not going to be an option anymore. I have like half a drink and I'll pass it off to my boyfriend because I have already had a buzz and will be in the hangover stage within 30 minutes.

The uncontrollable shits was aweful, and I'm glad I work with family. I'd stand up and there was just no control whatsoever over my bowels. I accidentally shit myself at my desk once and I felt disgusting (but who are we kidding, you're not a real adult until you shit your pants at least once accidentally, right?)

All that being said, after starting with 25mg, and being upped to 50mg, to my now after 3 years of messing around with it, 200mg dose life's been good. I've built a tolerance to it now and have a feeling ill be switching soon (Yay, not lol) but if you can ride through the side effects for the first while, it gets better. Clear communication with your doctor is well needed too!
